jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

Job Summary:

The Senior Mechanical Design Engineer is responsible for designing highly complex and cutting-edge optomechanical/optoelectronic subsystem box/blade assemblies. You will be working closely with teams across a wide array of disciplines including cryogenics, optics, electronics, and manufacturing. You will be expected to apply DFM principles on an everyday basis.  Strong design skills incorporating mechanics of materials, thermodynamics, electronics, and precision design principles are a must.

Responsibilities:

• Responsibilities will focus on subsystem box/blade design analogous to datacenter compute/networking switches repurposed for quantum computer. (i.e. box design, thermal management, and interconnects/fiber management).

• Ownership of designs from prototype to production.

• Expertise in Design for Manufacturability, Design for Assembly.

• Expertise with GD&T.

• Expertise with tolerance analysis methods.

• Generate and maintain process flow documentation.

• Conduct DFMEA, PFMEA & risk analysis heat maps.

• Rapid prototyping of designs.

• Generate & maintain BOM’s & build standards.

• Ability to execute basic structural and thermal analyses to down-select designs.

• Practicing proper engineering revision control, preferably with Solidwork PDM / Arena (PLM).

Experience/Qualifications:

• Experience in designing compute/networking servers and cable/fiber management for datacenters.

• Experience with design for sheet metal fabrication ,CNC machining, and relevant fabrication processes.

• Strong communication & interpersonal skills.

• Willingness to support colleagues to achieve team objectives.

• Exercises independent judgement.

• Willingness to be hands on, and drive objectives forward.

• Execution of deliverables against schedule & quality targets.

• Bachelors Degree or above in Mechanical Engineering or a relevant discipline.

• 2-6 years+ of experience, with experience in datacenter rack design is preferred.

• Preferred experience: Design system in cryogenic and vacuum environments is a plus.

• Preferred experience: Design for liquid cooling with cold plate assemblies is a plus.

jobs.title: Staff Compliance Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT LIVEKIT

LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

 


ABOUT THIS ROLE

Enterprise customers trust us with real-time audio, video and data belonging to their own end users, and before they build on LiveKit they want proof that we protect it. Our compliance program gives them that proof, and enterprise deals close on it. We are hiring a Compliance Engineer to lead the customer-facing side of that program. You will be the strategic partner to our sales team on security and compliance in enterprise deals, and you will own how we answer customers: security questionnaires, our answer library and the security terms in customer contracts.

You will join a small Trust team that covers security, IT and compliance, and you will own real parts of the program from your first week. You will share the day-to-day running of the compliance program with the rest of our Compliance team. We want someone who works themselves out of a job on the repeatable work. You will automate and simplify what you own, so your time goes to the larger deals and our compliance work grows more slowly than our customer base. We run SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS and HIPAA today, with ISO 9001 in progress. This role is remote, based in the United States or Canada.

 


YOU’LL THRIVE AT LIVEKIT IF YOU

 - automate the second time you do something by hand

 - like being in the room with a customer’s security team on a large deal

 - understand what a control is for and can tell when it is working

 - write clearly for auditors, engineers and customers alike

 - are a fast learner and thrive in ambiguity

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the strategic partner to our sales team on security and compliance: get into enterprise deals early and work directly with customers’ security teams.

 - Own customer security questionnaires, DDQs and our answer library, including the questionnaire automation we run in Vanta.

 - Advise on the security and compliance terms in customer contracts, working with our legal team.

 - Automate and simplify the repeatable work you own, and make common customer asks self-serve through our trust center and first-line support, working with IT and Customer Support.

 - Share the day-to-day running of the compliance program on a business-hours rotation: vendor reviews, policies, evidence collection, the risk register and questions from product and engineering.

 - Lead or support certification audits, working with our external auditors and with the engineering, IT and security teams that own the controls.

 


WHO YOU ARE

 - 5+ years in compliance engineering, GRC, customer trust or security assurance, with hands-on ownership of controls.

 - A track record of scaling a compliance service: you took a recurring workflow, cut the manual effort or turnaround, and can show the before and after.

 - Experience owning customer security questionnaires and DDQs for enterprise customers, working directly with a sales team on deals.

 - You like customer-facing work and have joined calls with customers’ security teams on large enterprise deals.

 - Hands-on experience with Vanta, including questionnaire automation and keeping tests and evidence healthy.

 - Experience managing an audit end to end with an external auditor.

 - The judgment to work from the intent of a control: you know where a requirement leaves room, and you can agree that with an auditor.

 - Scripting and automation skills in a language such as Python, and the ability to read cloud, identity and CI/CD configuration well enough to judge whether a control works.

 


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with PCI-DSS, ISO 9001, HIPAA, GDPR or the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.

 - Experience reviewing security and compliance terms in customer contracts.

 - Experience building AI-assisted workflows for compliance or customer assurance.

 - Experience advising product and engineering teams on compliance, or working in Kubernetes-native environments.

 - Third-party risk or sub-processor program experience.

 


OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU

 - An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world

 - Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - Health, dental, and vision benefits

 - Flexible vacation policy

 

LiveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

jobs.title: Associate Director, R&D IT (Contract)
jobs.description:
Attention recruitment agencies: All agency inquiries are vetted through 4DMT’s internal Talent Acquisition team. No unsolicited resumes will be accepted. The 4DMT Talent Acquisition team must expressly engage agencies on any requisition. Agencies contacting hiring managers directly will not be tolerated, and doing so may impact your ability to work with 4DMT in the future.

4DMT is a leading late-stage biotechnology company advancing durable and disease-targeted therapeutics with potential to transform treatment paradigms and provide unprecedented benefits to patients. The Company’s lead product candidate 4D-150 is designed to be a backbone therapy forming the foundation of treatment of blinding retinal vascular diseases by providing multi-year sustained delivery of anti-VEGF biologics (aflibercept and anti-VEGF-C) with a single intravitreal injection, which substantially reduces the treatment burden associated with current bolus injections. The Company’s lead indication for 4D-150 is wet age-related macular degeneration and the second indication is diabetic macular edema, which are both in Phase 3 development. The Company’s second product candidate is 4D-710, which is the first known genetic medicine to demonstrate successful delivery and expression of the CFTR transgene in the lungs of people with cystic fibrosis after aerosol delivery.

We are taking genetic medicine to new heights and into new disease areas to overcome challenges not addressed by existing medicines. This incredible challenge drives our relentless and talented team. Our people are the essence of our inspiring, innovative and collaborative environment that encourages individual contributions and provides opportunities for career development. We seek the best in the industry who identify with our mission and our bold and innovative results-driven approach. Our Core Values drive the way we work together:

• Dare to Cure

• Break Boundaries

• Beyond Yourself

• Prepare & Execute Relentlessly

Join us in creating the future of genetic medicine.

GENERAL SUMMARY

4D Molecular Therapeutics (4DMT) is a late-stage clinical gene therapy company advancing a potentially transformative pipeline toward its first Biologics License Application (BLA) and commercial launch. Reporting to the Sr. Director, IT Business Partner, R&D, the Associate Director, R&D IT, provides hands-on technology leadership and serves as the IT System Owner for assigned GxP and business-critical applications and initiatives supporting 4DMT organizations, including R&D, Technical Operations, Clinical Science and Operations, Data Sciences and Biostatistics, Quality Assurance (QA), Quality Control (QC), Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Program Management, Facilities, and Medical Affairs.

The role is accountable for the technical ownership, implementation, administration, integration, operation, security, support, inspection readiness, and lifecycle of an assigned portfolio of systems. The Associate Director provides portfolio leadership for assigned areas and connects functional needs to the integrated R&D roadmap. The Associate Director partners with Business Process Owners, QA, IT Computer System Validation (CSV), IT infrastructure teams, vendors, and implementation partners to ensure assigned systems are fit for intended use, appropriately validated, reliable, secure, and supportable.

This is a hands-on IT role requiring a balanced combination of technical knowledge, GxP system lifecycle experience, and project leadership. The Associate Director applies independent judgment to resolve complex system-level issues, leads interdependent technical and compliance workstreams, provides senior-level guidance for assigned applications, and supports the appropriate use of automation and approved AI technologies. The role operates within the Sr. Director's strategy, architecture, and governance.

MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Serve as the IT System Owner for an assigned portfolio of R&D platforms and GxP and business-critical applications, including laboratory systems such as LIMS, chromatography data systems, laboratory instrument software, and scientific data platforms, with accountability for technical health, regulatory readiness, operational performance, supportability, roadmap execution, and lifecycle outcomes.

• Manage demand intake for assigned areas, develop business cases, and provide portfolio reporting on status, spend, risks, and priorities.

• Partner with Business Process Owners to understand intended use, business processes, operational priorities, and user needs, and translate them into technology requirements, solution options, and recommendations.

• Partner with Quality Assurance and IT Computer System Validation to determine GxP applicability, system risk, validation strategy, required controls, testing approach, and lifecycle documentation while maintaining appropriate role independence.

• Lead complex system implementations, upgrades, integrations, migrations, remediation activities, and technology-enabled process improvements from evaluation through validated deployment and operational transition. Manage scope, schedule, risks, dependencies, approved budgets, and cross-functional workstreams.

• Administer or oversee application configuration, user accounts, security roles, interfaces, reports, scheduled processes, reference data, and other technical components within the authorized IT scope.

• Understand and maintain appropriate documentation of application architecture, hosting models, integrations, data flows, technical dependencies, identity and access controls, backup and recovery, business continuity, and vendor support arrangements.

• Ensure appropriate controls are established and maintained for electronic records and signatures, access, audit trails, data integrity, integrations, data migration, backup and recovery, retention, archival, change management, and vendor oversight.

• Serve as the senior IT escalation point for complex application, validation, integration, performance, instrument-interface, data-integrity, and vendor-performance issues, leading root-cause analysis and sustainable resolution.

• Maintain inspection-ready technical, validation, operational, and lifecycle documentation, represent IT in regulatory inspections and audits, and support supplier assessments, periodic reviews, deviations, CAPAs, and remediation activities for assigned systems.

• Lead and manage contractors, consultants, vendors, managed-service providers, and vendor resources supporting assigned systems and projects. Manage vendor budgets, forecasts, and service levels; establish priorities, deliverables, acceptance criteria, service expectations, and escalation paths; review performance and work quality; and ensure outsourced deliverables meet applicable technical, security, validation, documentation, and GxP requirements.

• Develop and manage lifecycle roadmaps for assigned applications and recommend upgrades, replacements, integrations, support-model improvements, and retirement. Identify appropriate opportunities to use workflow automation, low-code platforms, data tools, scripting, Microsoft Copilot, and other approved AI technologies to improve business processes and system operations.

• Lead cross-functional teams and mentor colleagues and system stakeholders in IT System Owner practices, application governance, validation partnership, operational support, inspection readiness, and vendor oversight.

• Support the AI Governance Council by providing technical input and helping assess and implement approved AI solutions for assigned systems and processes.

• Communicate system health, project status, risks, technical options, and investment needs to stakeholders, and escalate material portfolio, architecture, compliance, funding, security, and resource decisions to IT leadership

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline

• Advanced degree or relevant professional certification is preferred

Experience:

• 10+ years of progressive experience with a Bachelor’s degree or 6+ years with a Master’s degree, supporting, implementing, administering, validating, and managing business applications in a pharmaceutical, medical-device, or comparable regulated environment.

• 5+ years leading R&D applications and GxP operations.

• 2+ years leading vendors and project teams.

• Hands-on experience serving as the IT System Owner, application owner, system administrator, technical lead, product owner, or comparable role for multiple regulated or business-critical applications.

• Experience with the full lifecycle of GxP computerized systems, including requirements, implementation, validation, deployment, change control, operational support, periodic review, upgrades, and retirement.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex GxP technology initiatives involving multiple business, technical, quality, validation, security, integration, and vendor stakeholders.

• Experience collaborating with Business Process Owners, QA, CSV, IT infrastructure teams, vendors, and implementation partners, and making system-level risk and lifecycle recommendations.

• Experience with GxP systems and interfaces, IT QA, or Computer System Validation is strongly preferred.

• Demonstrated experience directing contractors, consultants, implementation partners, or managed-service resources, including setting priorities, reviewing deliverables, monitoring performance, resolving delivery issues, and ensuring technical quality and compliance.

Other Qualifications/Skills:

• Strong understanding of IT System Owner responsibilities and GxP computerized system controls, including 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, GAMP 5, ALCOA+ principles, and risk-based Computer Software Assurance practices.

• Ability to quickly understand application architecture, integrations, data flows, hosting models, security controls, technical dependencies, and support requirements.

• Ability to balance business needs, compliance requirements, technical risks, operational support, security, and cost when making system-level recommendations.

• Strong project leadership, technical problem-solving, vendor management, documentation, and stakeholder communication skills.

• Working knowledge of programming, scripting, databases, workflow automation, or low-code technology sufficient to evaluate solution designs, vendor approaches, and automated solutions is preferred.

• Experience using Microsoft Copilot or other approved artificial-intelligence tools to improve productivity, documentation, information management, or business processes is preferred.

• Portfolio and project management & senior-stakeholder communication skills.

• Ability to evaluate AI solutions with governance partners.

• Working knowledge of ICH E6(R3).

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:

• Physical Activity - Repetitive motions: Making substantial movements (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers. Fingering: Picking, pinching, typing or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than with whole hand or arm as in handling. Talking: Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.

• Physical Requirements - Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally, and all other sedentary criteria are met.

• Working Conditions - The worker is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions (as in typical office or administrative work).

Base salary compensation range: $89.00 - $104.00 / hour

Please note, the base salary compensation range and actual salary offered to the final candidate depends on various factors: candidate’s geographical location, relevant work experience, skills, and years of experience.

About Us

The Honest Company (NASDAQ: HNST) is a personal care company dedicated to creating cleanly-formulated and sustainably-designed products spanning categories across diapers, wipes, baby personal care, beauty, apparel, household care and wellness. Launched in 2012, the Company is on a mission to challenge ingredients, ideals, and industries through the power of the Honest brand, the Honest team, and the Honest Standard. For more information about the Honest Standard and the Company, please visit www.honest.com.

Our Mission

We're on a mission to empower people to live happy, healthy lives. We're a wellness brand with values rooted in consciousness, community, transparency, and design. Every day and in every way, we hold ourselves to an Honest standard. We believe that it is our responsibility to do our part to help create a healthy and sustainable future for all.

The Role

The Honest Company is seeking an experienced sales leader to join our Ecommerce team as a Director of Sales, responsible for our Amazon business. In this role, you will lead the strategic management and growth of the Amazon account across Health and Personal Care, Beauty and Fresh categories, driving brand presence, demand generation, and long-term, profitable sales performance. This role offers the opportunity to directly influence category growth, elevate brand impact, and contribute to Honest’s mission at scale.

If you are a results-driven sales professional who values purpose-led growth and thrives in a highly visible, fast-paced eCommerce environment, we encourage you to apply.

What you'll do:

• Partner with the VP of Ecommerce to translate Honest’s growth objectives into a clear Amazon account strategy, inclusive of annual operating plans, category roadmaps, and Joint Business Plans (JBPs).

• Own monthly, quarterly, and annual Amazon goals across revenue, net PPM, contribution margin, and market share.

• Serve as the primary owner of the Amazon relationship, leading day-to-day engagement with Vendor Manager(s) across Beauty, HPC, and Fresh business. Maintaining connectivity with DMMs and Amazon cross-functional teams as needed.

• Own full P&L responsibility for the Amazon business, actively managing Vendor Central financial levers including list price, trade terms, accruals, rebates, markdowns, shortages, and chargebacks to drive profitable growth.

• Lead JBP execution, trade investment strategy, and annual negotiations in close partnership with Finance and Trade, ensuring alignment to Honest financial targets and Amazon category priorities.

• Collaborate with Marketing team to plan, manage, and optimize Amazon Retail Media investments (Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display) to support key initiatives, promotional events, and new item launches.

• Use Vendor Central and third-party data platforms to analyze sales, profitability, share, traffic, and conversion, translating insights into clear actions across pricing, assortment, promotion, and media.

• Own demand forecasting for Amazon, delivering accurate weekly, monthly, and annual forecasts inclusive of promotional and trade activity, in partnership with Demand Planning and Supply Chain teams.

• Lead Amazon promotional execution across tentpole events and everyday programs, including Best Deals and Subscribe & Save, ensuring strong merchandising, operational readiness, and post-event reporting.

• Monitor category and competitive performance on Amazon, identifying risks and opportunities related to pricing, assortment, promotions, content, and share of voice, and communicate actionable insights to Sales, Brand, and Marketing partners.

• Provide regular business reporting and executive-level readouts, including weekly performance updates, monthly forecasts, and quarterly business reviews.

• Act as a cross-functional connector, ensuring alignment across Sales, Finance, Marketing, Retail Media, Supply Chain, and Content to deliver consistent execution on Amazon.

You'll love this job if you're:

• Thoughtfully articulate. You always know the best way to communicate and build strong relationships along the way.

• A confident, dynamic leader. You’re known far and wide for your impressive relationship building skills.

• Dedicated and fast moving. You’re known to operate with urgency, focus, discipline and discernment.

• A dynamite problem solver and project manager. You’re always thinking (at least) one step ahead.

What you'll need:

• Minimum 5+ years of direct and hands-on experience in a 1P Amazon Sales Lead role.

• Bachelor's Degree

• Experience working in a Consumer-Packaged Goods (CPG), Fast-Moving Consumer Good (FMCG) and/or consumer durables industry strongly preferred.

• Successfully led and executed 2+ annual vendor negotiations (AVNs).

• Ability to analyze syndicated data.

• Experience developing and managing trade budgets.

• Ability to operate independently given direction and bring ideas and solutions to issues raised.

• Expert level discernment; evaluates competing priorities and trade-offs with limited direction.

• History of negotiating complex business deals that provide value to all parties.

• Ability to analyze and assess organizational needs and provide solutions accordingly.

• Must excel at advanced analytics, identifying data needs and then articulating the data into a comprehensive story.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills; must be able to present data in an organized manner to executive levels of the organization with confidence.

• Strong project planning, tracking & organizing skills.

• Ability to create relationships and effectively collaborate with HQ team members from a remote location.

• Solid understanding of P&L management, gross margin and pricing structures, impact of discounting, and trade terms.

Compensation

The pay range for this role is $175,000 - $200,000. Actual compensation is based on many factors including but not limited to depth of experience, skill level, ability, knowledge, education, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The total rewards package for this position may also include base, annual incentive plan, benefits, retirement plan, equity, and Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

Benefits & Perks

jobs.title: Response Center Advocate - Students encouraged to APPLY
jobs.description:
As a Response Center Advocate, you'll help support individuals with disabilities and age-related needs through video monitoring and sensor technologies. Based out of our Mendota Heights office, you'll monitor activity, respond to alerts, communicate with individuals and support teams, and follow established protocols to ensure concerns are addressed promptly and appropriately.

• You'll also develop practical technology skills as you learn our systems and assist with basic technical support. You don't need an IT background to succeed. We're looking for someone with natural curiosity, problem-solving ability, and an interest in learning how technology works.

WHO ARE YOU?

• Are you naturally curious about technology? Do you enjoy figuring out how things work, learning new software, and finding solutions when something isn't quite right?
• We're looking for someone who brings a combination of people skills, technical curiosity, and a willingness to learn.
• You're comfortable navigating computers and software, and learning new technology doesn't intimidate you.
• When someone calls in a panic, you don't panic with them. You bring the calm, kindness, and a plan.
• You enjoy helping people and turning a frustrating situation into a better experience.
• You're resourceful and willing to ask questions, research solutions, and work through challenges.
• You're interested in developing your technical knowledge and potentially growing into opportunities within the IT or technology space.

Maybe you've always been the go-to person when family or friends need help with their computers, phones, or Wi-Fi. Perhaps you're currently taking IT classes, considering that career path, or simply enjoy learning about technology.

You don't need to know everything coming in. We'll teach you our systems. What matters most is your attitude, aptitude, and willingness to learn!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Be the Eyes & Ears: Monitor video cameras, sensors, and communication devices to help ensure the safety and well-being of the individuals we support.
• Jump Into Action: Respond to alerts by following established protocols, making calls, and coordinating with house staff, management, or local authorities when needed.
• Be the Friendly Voice: Answer calls, listen to concerns, and help individuals, caregivers, and team members work through questions or challenges.
• Play Tech Detective: Identify and troubleshoot basic technology issues involving cameras, devices, and connectivity. Recognize when additional technical support is needed and escalate more complex issues appropriately.
• Be the First Line of Tech Support: Assist teammates and end users with basic technology needs, including navigating systems, common computer issues, and password resets. Learn to use our internal ticketing system, SysAid, to document requests, track issues, and route them to the appropriate resources.
• Keep the Details in Check: Document activity, calls, and follow-ups in Salesforce. Accurately start and stop services to help keep billing on track.
• Keep Things Running Smoothly: Communicate important updates, maintain accurate handoffs, and ensure the next person has the information they need to support a seamless transition between shifts.

MUST HAVE:

• High school diploma or equivalent.
• At least 18 years of age.
• At least one year of hands-on experience engaging with customers, patients, students, or end users. Examples include call centers, hospitals/clinics, schools, hospitality, customer service, or technical support environments.
• Basic computer proficiency, including the ability to navigate multiple software applications, learn new technology platforms, follow technical instructions, and perform basic troubleshooting.
• Familiarity with Microsoft 365 applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint.

NICE TO HAVE:

• Interest in pursuing a career in IT, technology, or technical support, with current enrollment or plans to pursue coursework in Information Technology, Computer Science, Networking, or a related field.
• Experience with technology platforms, internet connectivity, or Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems such as Salesforce.
• Previous exposure to help desk support, ticketing systems, or basic technical troubleshooting.

SKILLS CRUCIAL TO SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE:

• People Person: You genuinely enjoy helping others and know that a little kindness, patience, and a friendly voice can make someone's day.
• Cool, Calm & Collected: When things get busy or an unexpected alert comes through, you stay composed, think things through, and take action.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Global Supply Chain, Commercial
jobs.description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

As Arc's Senior Manager Global Supply Chain, Commercial, you will own the end-to-end supply base for Arc's commercial vessels, from first RFQ through rate production. That means you'll build and lead a team of Global Supply Managers, set sourcing strategy for the commodities that define our commercial boats, and be the single supply chain voice for Commercial Programs leadership.

We're looking for someone fired up by the mission and ready to build. You'll thrive here if you move fast, take ownership, and care about the details.

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Los Angeles headquarters.

What You'll Do

Leading the team

• Building, hiring and developing a team of Global Supply Managers covering Commercial Programs commodities, including energy storage, powertrain, propulsion and high-voltage electronics, low-voltage and E/E components, mechanical components

• Setting clear commodity ownership, goals and operating rhythm, and coaching GSMs to run sourcing events and supplier relationships on their own

Owning sourcing strategy

• Developing category strategies for each commercial commodity: make vs. buy, single vs. dual source, domestic vs. global, and long-term agreement structure

• Leading sourcing for major systems such as propulsion units and generators, battery systems, power electronics and marine-class electrical equipment

• Running RFQs and negotiations end to end, from requirements definition with Engineering through award, contract and launch

• Negotiating supply agreements covering pricing, LTAs, capacity commitments, warranty, IP and payment terms

Delivering for programs

• Being the supply chain lead on Commercial Programs teams, owning parts readiness, should-cost and supplier risk from concept through rate production

• Building and maintaining supply plans for long-lead items, and pull procurement decisions early enough to protect vessel delivery dates

• Partnering with Engineering on design-for-cost and design-for-supply, and driving supplier involvement early in the design process

• Owning material cost targets for commercial vessels and reporting BOM cost, savings and risk to program and executive leadership

Managing the supply base

• Qualifying and onboarding new suppliers with Quality, including the documentation and traceability that class societies and commercial customers require

• Running supplier performance management: QBRs, scorecards, corrective actions and escalations on delivery, quality and cost

• Identifying and mitigating supply risk, including single-source exposure, lead-time volatility, tariffs and trade compliance, and supplier financial health

Building the function

• Help defining how Global Supply Chain works at Arc as we scale: processes, commodity classification, supplier data standards and tooling

• Driving clean, accurate parts and supplier data in our MRP so that planning and procurement can run on it

• Sharing learnings and standards across Recreational, Commercial and Defense so the whole supply base gets stronger

Minimum Qualifications

• 10+ years in supply chain, procurement or sourcing for complex engineered hardware (marine, automotive, aerospace, heavy equipment, energy or similar)

• 3+ years leading people, including hiring and developing sourcing or supply management professionals

• Track record of leading strategic sourcing for high-value systems from RFQ through award and production launch

• Strong commercial negotiation skills, with experience structuring long-term supply agreements, pricing models and capacity commitments

• Experience working directly with Engineering on new product introduction, including reading drawings, specifications and BOMs

• Working knowledge of cost modeling and should-cost analysis

• Comfortable working in MRP/ERP systems and building your own analysis in Excel or similar tools

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business or a related field, or equivalent experience

• Willing to travel domestically and internationally to suppliers, up to 25%

• This position requires access to information controlled under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Applicants must be a “U.S. person” as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.62), subject to review of the position’s actual access requirements and applicable law.

Bonus Qualifications

• Commercial marine or shipbuilding experience, including vessels built to ABS, DNV, Lloyd's Register or USCG requirements

• Sourcing experience in marine propulsion, gensets, large battery systems or power electronics

• Experience in electrification: EV, e-marine, energy storage or electric heavy equipment

• Experience at a startup or scaling manufacturer, building a supply chain function rather than inheriting one

• Background in tariffs, trade compliance, customs or Buy America-type domestic content requirements

• Experience leading an MRP/ERP implementation or a parts and supplier data cleanup

• Engineering degree, MBA, or a CPSM/CSCP certification

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base salary for this role is $200,000 annually

Highly competitive equity grants are included with full time offers. As well as semi-annual bonuses tied to your impact, not just your tenure.

Additionally, Arc offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

• Healthcare benefits — 99% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision

• Parental leave — 14 weeks fully paid for birthing and non-birthing parents

• Generous time off — Highly competitive PTO with an opportunity to earn more time with tenure

• Income protection — Life and disability insurance for all employees

• Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access

• Water fund — $500 for you to spend each year to get out on the water, however you choose

• Professional development — $500 annual reimbursement for professional development and a monthly AI stipend

• Safety Support — Annual reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe

• Captain training — Training and access to take Arc boats out with friends and family

• Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

• Relocation assistance — Available depending on role eligibility.

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

• Ownership over both your work and the company’s success

• Empathy for colleagues and for customers

• Humility in problem solving and collaboration

• Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly

• Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives.

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

jobs.title: Principal Executive Recruiter, R&D
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Principal Executive Recruiter at GitLab, you’ll lead VP-level and other senior leadership searches across Engineering, Product, Security, IT, Data, and other technical teams. You’ll partner directly with senior executives to identify, engage, assess, and hire leaders, bringing market intelligence and a research-driven approach to complex, often confidential searches. Alongside owning searches end to end, you’ll help shape the strategies, frameworks, and practices that strengthen executive recruiting at GitLab, balancing search rigor with the agility of a fast-moving technology organization.

What You’ll Do

• Lead VP-level and other senior leadership searches end to end, from search strategy and market mapping through assessment, selection, and closing.

• Advise C-suite executives and senior technical leaders on hiring decisions, challenge assumptions, and navigate complex stakeholder dynamics.

• Develop talent strategies using market mapping, competitive intelligence, creative sourcing, and recruiting data to guide each search.

• Build relationships with passive executive talent, understand their motivations, and connect opportunities to GitLab’s mission, technical vision, and business priorities.

• Partner with hiring leaders to define success profiles, assess executive capabilities and business impact, and guide evidence-based hiring decisions.

• Own executive candidate relationships and deliver a high-touch experience through compensation discussions, competing opportunities, and negotiations.

• Manage multiple confidential, business-critical searches with discretion, balancing urgency, quality, stakeholder alignment, and candidate experience.

• Collaborate with Talent Acquisition leadership and executive recruiting peers to improve search frameworks, assessment practices, reporting, and tools.

What You’ll Bring

• Experience independently leading VP-level and senior executive searches through successful hires in an executive search firm, an in-house executive recruiting function, or both.

• Executive recruiting experience across technical functions such as Engineering, Product, Security, Data, or Infrastructure, with the technical fluency and curiosity to learn new domains.

• The ability to build trusted relationships with C-suite executives, influence senior stakeholders, and provide candid, evidence-based guidance on hiring decisions.

• Skills in talent research, market mapping, creative sourcing, leadership assessment, and engaging and closing passive executive talent.

• Business judgment, communication, and negotiation skills to navigate sensitive searches, complex compensation discussions, and competing executive priorities.

• Experience developing or improving executive search methodologies, frameworks, and processes while maintaining speed and flexibility.

• A hands-on approach to managing multiple high-priority searches independently and working through ambiguity.

• Experience in high-growth technology or enterprise software organizations, global executive searches, and distributed organizations is helpful.

About the team

You’ll join a globally distributed, remote-first Talent Acquisition team where clear communication and reliable follow-through matter. Guided by GitLab’s operating principles, including Speed with Quality, Ownership Mindset, and Customer Outcomes, we take ownership, move with urgency and rigor, and focus on hiring outcomes that matter to our internal customers. We share learnings and create reusable resources to continually improve the quality and consistency of hiring across Business teams.

I also swapped “business acumen” for “technical fluency” since that’s the skill that matters most when assessing technical leaders. Everything else stays the same. If you’d like, I can also add language about assessing technical depth, such as architecture, engineering org design, or scaling teams, to the success profile bullet.

jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft GNC Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR SPACECRAFT GNC ENGINEER II

Based out of Rocket Lab’s site in Littleton, CO, the Senior Spacecraft GNC Engineer II is responsible for leading GNC and ADCS development for Rocket Lab’s growing fleet of diverse spacecraft. You will demonstrate a firm grasp of spacecraft GNC concepts and applications. You will work with all facets of the engineering life cycle: spacecraft concept and algorithm development, flight software implementation, subsystem requirements development, detailed GNC design, subsystem integration & test (I&T), and vehicle I&T. You will be responsible for planning and maintaining the development schedule to support the Space Systems Software organization in executing leading edge programs and products. You will work closely with related teams, including Systems, Avionics, Flight Software, Mission Operations, and Ground Software. You will also directly interact with customers to ensure mission success.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Mentor a team responsible for GNC design, modeling, and analysis for a wide variety of spacecraft and space missions to include LEO, MEO, GEO, Lunar, Interplanetary, Reentry, and RPOD

• Design of flight software, algorithms, and simulation product

• Development of spacecraft autonomy tools for constellation management

• GNC component selection and GNC subsystem design

• Test process development and execution

• Define fault detection and response

• Hardware-in-the-loop and Monte Carlo simulation

• Integration of flight and simulation software with modern analysis, test, and operations tools

• Support internal and external design reviews

• Work with department leads and program managers to plan and maintain team schedule and milestones and report technical status

• Coordinate with teams in Long Beach, CA and New Zealand

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• B.S and 8+ years of industry experience in GNC/ADCS

• Ability to maintain and obtain a security clearance

• Prior experience directly interfacing with aerospace customers in the commercial or government sectors

• U.S citizenship is required, due to program requirements

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• MS or PhD

• Active TS/SCI clearance

• 2+ years of RPOD design and operations experience

• Experience in Jira planning and workflow

• Prior experiencing mentoring a team of younger engineers

• Hands-on experience with IMU, reaction wheels, star trackers, gyroscopes, and other GNC hardware

• Experience developing blended attitude solutions from a variety of sensor data

• Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and verifying flight software

• Demonstrated experience with spacecraft on-orbit operations and anomaly resolution

• Prior experience leading a team across a project lifecycle (not necessarily a spacecraft, not necessarily a whole GNC system)

• Prior experience working multiple projects simultaneously and determining priorities for a team

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter (Cape Canaveral)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

TECHNICAL RECRUITER

RESPONSIBILITIES:

As a SpaceX recruiter, you will run a full desk with a variety of duties and responsibilities focused on the sourcing, screening, interviewing, and onboarding of top talent candidates to fill mission critical positions. In many cases, you are candidates’ first encounter with SpaceX and it is your job to represent the company with professionalism, pride, and enthusiasm. We work in teams and focus on collaboration yet require a high degree of autonomy. So, while you are not expected to simply go it alone, you are expected to show initiative, take responsibility, and run with tasks to completion.

Your day-to-day routine will change often as hiring priorities shift, but there is a basic set of activities you can expect to run with daily, including, but not limited to:

• Meet with your client groups to discuss headcount, new requisitions, hiring strategy, and/or interview feedback – you truly act as a partner to your clients and not merely as an order taker

• Screen candidates who apply to requisitions – as the SpaceX name brand grows, our job postings continue to fill up with stellar candidates

• Source candidates – often the best candidates are the ones not actively looking

• Discuss candidates you have screened with your client groups and recommend top candidates for interviews

• Give tours to candidates before their onsite

• Attend interviews alongside your client groups to act as another set of eyes and ears in evaluating candidates

• Once candidates are approved for hire, you will begin the offer process including initiating background checks, negotiating offer packages and extending offer letters

Some days you will have multiple candidates coming onsite for interviews and you will spend that time giving tours and coordinating the candidate experience. Other days, you will need to fill your candidate pipeline and will spend the majority of the day screening/sourcing candidates. No day is the same here and the pace moves fast, but ultimately your job is to effectively attract, organize, and manage the flow of the country’s most talented individuals.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree and 1+ years of recruiting experience; or associate degree and 2+ years of experience; or 3+ years of professional experience as a recruiter in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 2+ years of technical recruiting experience

• 2+ years of SGA recruiting experience

• Experience with in-house recruiting

• Experience with high volume recruiting

• Experience recruiting electrical, mechanical and aerospace engineers

• Experience recruiting skilled labor

• Strong tenure with demonstrated success in recruiting roles

• Full life cycle recruiting experience, from sourcing to closing

• Comfort with reviewing, evaluating and reporting on recruiting data

• Ability to distinguish between the top 50% and the top 5% of talent within their respective fields

Senior Validation Engineer Responsibilities:

• Review the URS, Functional Specification, equipment specifications, design documentation, and site requirements to establish a risk-based CQV strategy, including facility, utility, RABS/LAF, and computerized system prerequisites.

• Perform a documented gap assessment of the vendor qualification package (FAT, SAT, and IQ/OQ) to determine what can be leveraged, and develop and execute supplemental wrap-around IQ/OQ protocols for requirements not adequately covered.

• Support installation verification and SAT, including equipment connections, utilities, instrumentation, facility interfaces, and network and environmental/particle monitoring interfaces.

• Execute OQ testing of filling and dosing accuracy, pump operation, calibration verification, syringe and cap infeed, screw-tip/capping functionality, reject mechanisms, recipes, controls, alarms, interlocks, emergency stops, and safety functions.

• Verify computerized system functionality, including user access management, role-based permissions, electronic records, audit trails, report generation, and network connectivity, along with data integrity and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.

• Perform RABS/LAF qualification activities to verify the ISO 5 critical filling environment within the ISO 7 background room, including HEPA certification and airflow documentation review, airflow parameter verification, and dynamic airflow visualization/smoke studies under representative operating conditions and interventions.

• Develop and execute PQ protocols for the 3 mL, 5 mL, and 10 mL syringe formats, evaluating filling accuracy, equipment performance, changeover functionality, and representative or worst-case operating conditions against approved acceptance criteria.

• Review execution records, document and help resolve discrepancies and deviations, and prepare final qualification reports and the closeout package, coordinating with facility modification and utility commissioning teams to confirm prerequisite systems are qualified first.

Job Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Science, or a related technical field.

• 7+ years of CQV experience in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical device environment, with sterile or aseptic fill-finish experience.

• Hands-on experience qualifying automated filling and capping/closing equipment, including SAT, IQ, OQ, PQ, and format or change-part qualification.

• Experience with RABS, isolator, or LAF qualification, including HEPA certification review, airflow visualization/smoke studies, and ISO 5/ISO 7 cleanroom environments.

• Experience performing vendor documentation gap assessments and developing wrap-around protocols, with working knowledge of GAMP 5 and risk-based approaches such as ASTM E2500.

• Working knowledge of computerized system validation and data integrity for equipment controls, including 21 CFR Part 11, user access, and audit trail requirements.

• Strong technical writing, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to work independently and coordinate with vendors and cross-functional teams.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

As Arc's IT Engineer, Cloud Security, you will own the security architecture and infrastructure that protects Arc's systems, data, and people as we scale. You'll design, build, and operate secure cloud environments, networks, and identity systems, balancing strong security with the speed and flexibility our teams need to execute.

You'll work across cloud infrastructure, network security, identity and access management, endpoint security, and automation. You'll implement modern security practices like zero-trust access, infrastructure as code, and centralized identity management, while making our systems easier to manage and harder to compromise. As Arc expands into defense, you'll also help build and maintain the secure environments required to protect controlled information and meet government security standards.

This is a senior, hands-on role with broad ownership over Arc's security infrastructure. We're looking for someone who can design the right architecture, implement it themselves, and continuously improve it as the business grows.

You'll thrive here if you move fast, take ownership, and care about the details.

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Los Angeles headquarters.

jobs.title: Build and Test Engineer
jobs.description:
About Critical Energy
Critical Energy is an innovative, early-stage, venture-backed cleantech company on a mission to accelerate the global energy transition through abundant, low-cost clean energy. Founded by an ex-SpaceX engineer, Critical Energy designs and manufactures factory-built, modular power plants. These rapidly deployable systems convert heat into electricity using a closed-loop thermodynamic cycle and can be installed in just weeks.

Critical Energy’s technology delivers high-efficiency, 24/7 power for geothermal applications and waste heat recovery (including from data center gas turbines), making clean energy practical and cost-effective for demanding sectors like AI hyperscalers and data centers. Backed by top climate and technology investors, Critical Energy is scaling rapidly.

 

Our Mission:

To build an abundant, low-cost, 100% clean energy future through groundbreaking geothermal innovation.

We are a team of passionate engineers, designers, and visionaries building cutting-edge solutions to meet the world’s energy needs with 100% clean energy. We are in the initial stages of development and building our team. This is your chance to join on the ground floor of something big! If you are ready to work at a fun, fast-paced, groundbreaking organization that is positioned to revolutionize geothermal energy, apply today!

About the Role:
Critical Energy is hiring a Build & Test Engineer to build, integrate, and test our power plant hardware in our Hawthorne shop. You'll take systems from machined parts and vendor components to running hardware: turbomachinery, generators, pumps, heat exchangers, piping, valves, and instrumentation. Assembling hardware, writing test procedures from systems requirements, running the tests, and reporting the results.

Responsibilities:

 - Build and integrate pilot and demo units, from mechanical assembly through piping, fittings, and instrumentation installs

 - Assemble and align rotating equipment, including turbines, generators, and pumps

 - Inspect incoming parts from machine shops and vendors before they go into a build

 - Turn test plans from Systems into step-by-step procedures, then run tests on components, subsystems, and full systems, from leak and pressure checks through full-system runs

 - Install, calibrate, and check out sensors and test data acquisition, working with Controls on instrumentation and the control system

 - Own data quality and the first look at results: write test reports and work anomalies through root cause and close-out with the design owner

 - Feed build and test findings back to design through redlines, issue reports, and design changes

 - Design fixtures, tooling, and quick hardware mods in CAD, and get them made

 - Capture build lessons in work instructions and travelers, working with Manufacturing, so builds stay repeatable as we scale

 - Support factory acceptance testing and on-site commissioning at customer sites

 - Help shape and follow safe practices for work around pressurized systems and rotating machinery

Qualifications

 - Support development, qualification, and acceptance testing of reactor components, subsystems, and integrated hardware.

 - Develop and execute test plans and procedures to evaluate engineering requirements, hardware performance, and system reliability.

 - Assemble and operate test setups, including mechanical hardware, fluid systems, instrumentation, and data acquisition equipment.

 - Conduct test operations, monitor system behavior, and troubleshoot unexpected results or hardware issues.

 - Collaborate with mechanical, thermal, fluid systems, electrical, and controls engineers to develop test methods and resolve technical challenges.

 - Collect and analyze experimental data, compare results with engineering predictions, and support root cause investigations.

 - Identify test hazards, follow safety procedures, and support test readiness and risk mitigation activities.

 - Document test results, maintain test procedures, and recommend improvements to hardware, test methods, and processes.


Preferred Qualifications:

 - Strong engineering fundamentals in at least one area such as fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, mechanical systems, or electrical systems.

 - Experience developing or executing engineering tests, experimental methods, or hardware validation activities.

 - Experience with test instrumentation, data acquisition, troubleshooting, or engineering data analysis.

Ability to document technical work, solve engineering problems, and communicate findings across engineering disciplines.

Compensation

Actual base salary offered will be determined by: experience, skills, and work location. This range is for base salary, our total compensation includes equity and benefits. We welcome you to apply even if your expectations are outside our listed range.

jobs.title: DSP Engineer (Platform)
jobs.description:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array and parabolic ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.



Role: 

A satellite pass gives you a limited window to acquire the signal, track it as Doppler shifts the carrier frequency, and recover data as signal conditions change. As a DSP Engineer at Northwood, you’ll own the modem algorithms that make those links work on our next-generation radio platform.

You’ll take the modem from waveform definition and prototyping through real-time implementation on our in-house SDR and FPGA platform. You’ll decide how the signal-processing chain comes together, where each function runs, and how to measure performance under realistic channel conditions. You’ll work closely with RF, FPGA, and systems engineers to integrate your design and see how your algorithm choices translate into link performance across Northwood’s satellite ground network.


Responsibilities: 

 - Own the definition and development of modem algorithms end-to-end, from requirements through implementation and validation

 - Define waveform processing chains — synchronization, pulse shaping, equalization, and related signal-processing functions — for implementation on an in-house SDR platform or FPGA

 - Partition and implement modem signal-processing functions across FPGA logic and embedded/host-based compute, working within the existing hardware platform

 - Collaborate with RF, FPGA, and systems engineers to integrate modem algorithms into the end-to-end system and validate performance

 - Develop and run communication system tests to characterize modem performance under realistic channel impairments



Basic Qualifications: 

 - Bachelor's degree with 0-4 years of relevant experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field

 - Experience developing modems or waveform processing chains for SDR, wireless communications, radar, or similar RF systems

 - Strong understanding of digital communications theory: CCSDS waveforms, BPSK/QPSK/OQPSK, DVB-S2, carrier synchronization, pulse shaping, equalization, and Doppler effects

 - Demonstrated ability to carry waveform algorithms from analysis and prototyping through to a working implementation, rather than stopping at simulation

 - Working understanding of the complete signal chain and how modem design decisions interact with RF and hardware constraints

 - Experience with communication system testing and performance characterization



Preferred Qualifications: 

 - Experience with bit-equivalence verification through FPGAs

 - Familiarity with SDR frameworks such as GNU Radio

 - Experience with real-time signal processing

 - Systems programming skills in C++ or Rust, with Rust especially valued

 - Experience with beamforming, radar, or electronic warfare (EW) systems



Additional Information:



To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.



Northwood Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Northwood Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. 



If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know at accommodations@northwoodspace.io

jobs.title: CFD Engineer III/IV - Weapons Performance
jobs.description:
At Zone 5 Technologies, we're redefining what's possible in precision weapons and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). Our team of engineers and innovators are developing cutting-edge autonomous solutions to deliver affordable and scalable precision weapons, interceptors, and UAS.

We're building the next generation of munitions and unmanned systems for the United States and its allies. If you're driven by hard problems, energized by rapid innovation, and ready to make an impact on defense technology, you belong here.

We are currently looking for a CFD Engineer III/IV to join our Weapons Performance team. In this role, you will perform computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis to characterize the aerodynamic and ballistic performance of Zone 5’s air-launched effects, tactical interceptors, and next-generation munitions — from early concept and trade studies through wind tunnel and flight test correlation. You will work alongside the team’s senior engineers, executing analysis against established methods and standards while partnering closely with Design, Propulsion, GNC, Analysis, and Systems Engineering to ensure our systems perform reliably under demanding launch, flight, and terminal conditions.

Responsibilities:

• Perform high-fidelity CFD analysis across speed regimes typical to the defense industry to characterize aerodynamic performance — drag, lift, moment coefficients, and stability derivatives — for air-launched effects, tactical interceptors, and munitions.

• Generate meshes and conduct grid convergence studies for complex, high-speed vehicle geometries, including store separation and multi-body overset configurations.

• Support CFD-based aerodynamic database development used in GNC flight control law development, trajectory simulation, and mission performance analysis.

• Validate CFD results against wind tunnel and flight test data, and support root-cause investigation of discrepancies between simulation and test.

• Support store separation and safety-critical certification analysis for new and existing weapon systems.

• Run automated workflows and scripts for batch HPC job generation, post-processing, and data reduction, following established team procedures.

• Prepare technical reports and documentation of analysis results, including support for design reviews (PDR, CDR).

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in aerospace engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field required; Master's degree typical for candidates at this level, though exceptional applied experience can substitute.

• 5+ years of experience performing CFD analysis in an applied, product-centric, program-driven environment.

• Proficiency with CFD solvers commonly used in aerospace/defense aerodynamics (e.g., CFD++, OVERFLOW, Kestrel, FUN3D, STAR-CCM+, or ANSYS Fluent) for compressible, high-speed flow, along with the required meshing and geometry preparation tools.

• Proficiency with a CAD package (e.g., SolidWorks, CATIA, or Siemens NX) for aerodynamic modeling and CFD surface geometry preparation.

• Proficiency with CFD post-processing and visualization tools such as ANSYS Workbench, STAR-CCM+, other commercial tools, and/or ParaView.

• Experience characterizing aerodynamic performance of missiles, munitions, rockets, or other high-speed vehicles, including store separation and other aerodynamic effects.

• Experience validating and correlating CFD results against wind tunnel or flight test data.

• Programming or scripting proficiency (Python, MATLAB, or similar) for CFD automation, post-processing, and data reduction.

• Working knowledge of Linux environments and HPC cluster job scheduling sufficient to run and troubleshoot CFD workloads.

• Experience with version control (e.g., Git, SVN) for CFD codebases and associated automation scripts.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. DoD Secret security clearance; must qualify as a U.S. Person under ITAR regulations.

Level III: $120,000 - $149,000/yr.

Level IV: $149,000 - $182,000/yr.

$120,000—$182,000 USD

What's in it for you:

Benefits:

• Competitive total compensation package

• Comprehensive benefit package options include medical, dental, vision, life, and more.

• 401k with company-match

• 3 weeks of paid time off each year

• 40 hours of sick time

• 12 annual company holidays

Why Join Zone 5 Technologies?

• Innovative Environment: Work on cutting-edge technology that is shaping the future of defense and aerospace.

• Collaborative Culture: Join a team of passionate professionals dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

• Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

If you are passionate about unmanned aircraft technology and want to be a part of a dynamic and growing company, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and join the Zone 5 Technologies team!

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

jobs.title: Spacecraft GNC Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SPACECRAFT GNC ENGINEER II

Based out of Rocket Lab’s site in Littleton, CO, the Spacecraft GNC Engineer II is responsible for leading GNC and ADCS development for Rocket Lab’s growing fleet of diverse spacecraft. You will demonstrate a firm grasp of spacecraft GNC concepts and applications. jobs.title: Global Head of Pathology, Preclinical Safety
jobs.description:
Provides strategic, scientific, and organizational leadership for the global Pathology function within Preclinical Safety. Establishes the vision and strategy for Pathology and ensures that world-class pathology expertise, laboratory sciences, technologies, and capabilities are effectively deployed to support AbbVie’s discovery and development portfolio. Accountable for the quality, timeliness, consistency, and scientific impact of pathology insights that inform safety assessment, portfolio decisions, regulatory strategy, and the advancement of safe and effective medicines. Leads the Pathology organization through two major areas of accountability, Pathology Portfolio Advancement and Pathology Laboratory Sciences, each led by a Senior Director. Serves as a member of the Preclinical Safety Leadership Team and contributes broadly to functional strategy, portfolio priorities, talent, organizational capability, resource allocation, and the continued evolution of Preclinical Safety.

Key Responsibilities

• Establish and execute the global vision, scientific strategy, and long-term direction for Pathology within Preclinical Safety, ensuring that the function anticipates evolving portfolio needs, emerging modalities, regulatory expectations, and advances in pathology science and technology.
• Lead the global Pathology organization through the Senior Director, Pathology Portfolio Advancement and the Senior Director, Pathology Laboratory Sciences; establish clear accountability across the two pillars while ensuring strong integration of portfolio-facing pathology, laboratory sciences, and enabling capabilities.
• Ensure pathology expertise and resources are deployed across the discovery and development portfolio according to program risk, complexity, and business priority; provide senior scientific oversight and serve as the final escalation point for complex, novel, or potentially program-limiting pathology findings.
• Provide senior scientific counsel regarding the implications of pathology findings for candidate selection, study strategy, human relevance, mechanistic evaluation, regulatory strategy, governance decisions, and overall benefit-risk assessment.
• Establish global expectations and governance for scientific quality, consistency, peer review, interpretation, terminology, documentation, report quality, data integrity, GLP compliance, and regulatory readiness across internal and externally conducted pathology activities.
• Provide strategic oversight of pathology laboratory sciences, including histology, clinical pathology, and digital/computational pathology; sponsor capability and infrastructure investments that address meaningful scientific, portfolio, quality, and operational needs.
• Champion innovation in pathology, including quantitative image analysis, AI-enabled digital pathology, advanced safety biomarkers, translational approaches, and other emerging technologies that improve scientific insight, quality, consistency, or efficiency.
• Build and sustain a high-performing global organization by attracting, developing, and retaining outstanding scientific and leadership talent; coach senior leaders, strengthen succession pipelines, preserve critical expertise, and foster a culture of scientific rigor, inclusion, constructive challenge, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.
