jobs.title: Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
MISSION 💪

Our mission is to ensure that no one in the world has to suffer from a treatable skin disease because of an access issue ever again.




ABOUT HONEYDEW 👋

Honeydew https://honeydewcare.com/ is building a platform for hundreds of millions of people globally to access expertise and science-backed skin treatments, from prescription to retail.

Our tech-forward dermatology experience helps people with chronic skin conditions access licensed specialists, FDA-approved treatment, and ongoing support in record time (24 hours vs an industry average of 6 months).

Honeydew is the future of skin health — digitally native, scientifically rooted, integrated end-to-end (evaluation + treatments + lab tests), and powered by AI.




BRING YOUR EXPERIENCE TO CARE THAT ACTUALLY WORKS

As a Care Coordinator at Honeydew, you'll be the steady, skilled voice guiding patients through their treatment. You've done chat-based care before, so you already know what great written support looks like. Here, you'll put that experience to work from day one, helping patients feel heard, supported, and confident while keeping their care moving.

This role is built for someone ready to hit the ground running. You're comfortable with ambiguity, you like having clear metrics to hit, and you take pride in owning your queue.




YOUR DAY-TO-DAY

 - Manage a full patient caseload through app chat, writing clear, warm, professional messages (this is 99% of your patient interaction)

 - Own your response times and quality metrics, consistently meeting our SLAs

 - Anticipate patient questions and resolve issues in as few touchpoints as possible

 - Coordinate with pharmacies and labs by phone to troubleshoot prescription issues, insurance hiccups, and delivery problems

 - Connect with dermatology providers as needed to keep care plans on track

 - Keep meticulous records, because details matter when it's someone's health on the line

 - Monitor patient progress through ongoing messaging, troubleshoot obstacles, and celebrate wins along their journey

 - Share feedback on workflows and patient trends to help us improve how we deliver care




SCHEDULE

This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week role beginning on day one. Our patients reach out for support seven days a week, and weekend coverage is an important part of making sure their care never stalls. You'll work one of the following schedules:


Wednesday to Sunday, 12:00 PM to 10:00 PM ET
Saturday to Wednesday, 12:00 PM to 10:00 PM ET


We'll confirm your preferred schedule during the phone screen. During your shifts, you'll be expected to respond to patient messages within 4 hours.



You Might Be Our Person If…

 - You've been the go-to person on a chat support team and you're ready for a role that recognizes that

 - You're energized by clear goals and metrics, and you know how to hit them without sacrificing quality

 - You're comfortable with ambiguity and can keep things moving while processes are still being built

 - You can read tone and emotion in written messages and respond appropriately

 - You genuinely like people, even when they're frustrated and it's coming through in ALL CAPS

 - You'd rather proactively solve a problem than wait for a template

 - You believe healthcare should be accessible to everyone, not just the privileged few




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The Non-Negotiables:

 - At least 2 years of experience as a chat-based Care Coordinator, care specialist, or similar role (written chat support, not phone-based)

 - Comfort working in a fast-paced, metric-driven environment with clear SLAs

 - Comfort with ambiguity and shifting priorities

 - You're an exceptional writer: clear, warm, and professional in every message

 - You type at least 40 WPM

 - Availability to work full-time from day one, 40 hours per week, 5 days a week within 12:00 PM to 10:00 PM ET window.

 - A laptop or desktop computer (Mac or PC). Phones, Chromebooks, and iPads aren't supported.

 - Reliable internet and a private workspace. HIPAA compliance isn't optional.

 - You thrive working independently and take feedback as fuel, not criticism

 - High school diploma or equivalent




STRONG PREFERENCE FOR:

 - Experience at a healthcare or digital health startup

 - A healthcare or clinical support background, including familiarity with pharmacies, labs, or insurance

 - Experience with Slack, Zoom, and Google Workspace




WE’RE OFFERING:

 - Hourly pay: $21.63 - $24.04/hour (final pay is based on experience and skills)

 - Fully remote role

 - Direct impact you can measure

 - Ability to grow within the company

 - Great health, vision, and dental insurance

 - 401k with company match

 - One Medical, Kindbody, Talkspace, and HealthAdvocate membership

 - Unlimited time off

 - $100 monthly tech stipend

 - Free Honeydew membership

 - Direct access to new dermatology treatments

 - 20% off Honeydew products

 - Peer-to-peer recognition through Motivosity



Our Process

 - Application

 - Required online assessment through our partner Criteria, sent to your email after you apply. It covers typing and a few job-related skills. The assessment must be completed within 72 hours of receiving it, and applications without a completed assessment won't be considered for the role.

 - Phone screen with Recruiting (20 to 30 minutes)

 - Video interview with a member of the hiring team, including a short live written assessment over shared screen (30 minutes total)

 - Final video interview with another senior member of the team (30 minutes)

 - Offer



Candidates must be authorized to work for any employer in the US. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.



Candidates residing in the following states will be considered for this role: AL, AZ, CT, DC, FL, GA, ID, LA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NJ, NY, NC, OH, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI

jobs.title: Business Development Executive, NA Private Sector
jobs.description:
BUILD A SAFER WORLD.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

You will open doors at the North American private-sector financial institutions and crypto businesses TRM most needs in its network, so that senior conversations turn into the first qualified opportunity for an Account Director. 

This is a senior individual contributor role in the Strategic Accounts team, built around a network you have already earned rather than a closing quota. You hand each opportunity to the Account Director at demo and step back after trial, with AI doing the account research and pipeline upkeep so your time goes to the conversations only you can have.

The impact you will have:

 - Your relationships decide which North American financial institutions TRM reaches this year: you turn a senior network into first meetings, using AI research agents to prepare each account's structure, recent news, regulatory posture, and likely stakeholders before the first conversation.

 - TRM stays in the room when a champion leaves, because you build relationships across compliance, investigations, risk, and digital asset teams, and use AI to map stakeholders and flag coverage gaps in each named account.

 - You create the first qualified opportunity in accounts that standard coverage has not cracked, and hand it to the Account Director at demo with an AI-assisted account brief, so the AD starts from context.

 - TRM earns a seat at conferences, panels, and practitioner forums through your voice, and you use AI to turn event overlap and hallway conversations into tracked follow-ups within days.

 - Pipeline data stays current without manual upkeep: you use AI workflows across Salesforce and Gong notes to log activity and surface patterns across your network, such as recurring objections and rising interest.

 - What you hear in the field reaches Product, Marketing, and Policy quickly, because you summarize market and regulatory signal with AI and share it as short, structured notes.

What we’re looking for:

 - A deep, credible network across North American financial institutions or crypto infrastructure firms, ideally as a former head of digital assets at a bank or a senior BD owner at a custody or settlement provider, with AI-assisted tools to keep that network mapped and current.

 - A track record of turning relationships into real, trackable pipeline, not only warm introductions, with clean Salesforce records kept through AI-assisted logging.

 - Comfort as a public voice for TRM at conferences, panels, and practitioner forums, with AI-assisted prep for talking points and follow-up.

 - A concrete, repeatable AI workflow you can walk through, such as a real account where AI research changed how you approached the conversation.

 - Experience building senior relationships across several functions in one account, and using AI to keep stakeholder maps current.

 - Based in the United States (NYC preferred), willing to travel 30-40% for conferences and in-person account work, and comfortable using AI tools every week to plan travel and prepare each meeting.

About the Team:

 - You join Elias Kokaly's Strategic Accounts team, a small, senior group focused on unlocking TRM's hardest named accounts.

 - The BDE function is growing by region and segment, so you will have peers opening doors in other markets and a shared playbook to improve together.

 - The work is intellectually demanding: the people you meet are senior, the buying groups are large, and your credibility has to hold up in every conversation.

 - You collaborate closely with Account Directors, Pathfinders, Product, and Marketing, and you share what works so the whole team benefits.

Team Operating Rhythms:

 - Distributed, not distant: the team works across time zones. Your time zone is United States based (NYC preferred), with overlap hours to be confirmed by the hiring manager.

 - Communication is written first: clear, brief updates in Slack and Salesforce, with live time reserved for account strategy and customer conversations.

 - Regular account reviews with the hiring manager and the regional sales head decide which doors to open next, with cadence to be confirmed at intake.

 - Handoffs are explicit: opportunities move to the Account Director at demo, and the BDE steps back after trial, with no account splits or quota overlap.

Travel Requirements:

 - Schedule: 30-40% travel for conferences and in-person account work.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

 - Within 30 days, a mapped list of named North American accounts and the senior relationships you can activate, so first outreach starts in week two instead of month two.

 - Within 60 days, the first senior meetings booked inside strategic accounts that coverage has not reached, each with an AI-prepared stakeholder map and a clear next step.

 - Within 90 days, the first BDE-sourced opportunity handed to an Account Director at demo with a complete account brief, so the AD can book a trial without repeating discovery.


APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.




INTERVIEWING WITH TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

 - Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

 - Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

 - First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

 - Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

 - References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

 - Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

 - Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.




AI FLUENCY AT TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

 - Accelerate repeatable workflows

 - Structure and solve problems

 - Improve output quality

 - Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.




LIFE AT TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

 - Priorities and targets to change quickly

 - Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

 - A high level of personal ownership and accountability

 - Close collaboration across teams and functions

 - Frequent, high-touch communication

 - Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

 - A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 




LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

 - Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

 - Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

 - Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.





JOIN OUR MISSION

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

As part of the Akido medical network, we are currently responsible for more than 250,000 patients in Southern California, with plans to expand into new markets across the U.S. We care deeply about the communities we serve and are committed to providing accessible, high quality healthcare that helps our patients and communities live their fullest lives. We hope you’ll join our team

The Opportunity
Chaparral Medical Group is recruiting for a General Neurologist to join our team to deliver comprehensive outpatient neurological care. You’ll play a critical role in diagnosing, treating, and managing a broad range of neurological conditions in a fully outpatient setting. You will work closely with a multidisciplinary team to deliver exceptional care, supported by a well-established referral network, and help improve neurological health outcomes in our community.

We welcome applicants at all career stages, from recent residency and fellowship graduates to experienced neurologists.

What You’ll Do

• Evaluate, diagnose and manage patients with a wide array of neurological conditions in the outpatient setting, including headache and migraine, epilepsy and seizure disorders, neuropathy, movement disorders, dementia and cognitive impairment, multiple sclerosis, and stroke follow-up

• Perform comprehensive neurological examinations and order and interpret diagnostic tests, including neuroimaging, EEG, and EMG/nerve conduction studies

• Develop individualized treatment plans for patients with chronic and complex neurological conditions

• Manage long-term medication therapy and monitor for side effects and treatment response

• Monitor patient outcomes and adjust treatment plans based on progress and evolving needs

• Provide patient and family education on diagnosis, treatment options, and lifestyle modifications

• Collaborate closely with primary care providers, specialists, and allied health professionals to ensure coordinated care

• Maintain thorough and timely patient documentation in the EMR system

• Stay current with advancements in neurology through continuing education, research, and peer collaboration

• Contribute and advise on possible improvements to the EMR system, actively collaborating with the tech team on future product enhancements

Who You Are

jobs.title: Clinical Trial Associate
jobs.description:
Eikon Therapeutics is a new biopharmaceutical company employing revolutionary technology at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, computation, and biology to discover novel treatments for life-threatening diseases. Eikon’s discovery platform is built on groundbreaking innovations from its founders (Nobel Prize, 2014), culminating in the creation of microscopes which enable real time, molecular-resolution measurements of protein movement in living cells, thereby unlocking otherwise intractable classes of proteins as drug targets.

Position

As a Clinical Trials Associate in Oncology, you will play a crucial role in supporting the planning, coordination, and execution of Phase I-III insourced global clinical studies within the oncology portfolio. Operating in a dynamic and collaborative environment, you will provide essential support for the execution of clinical trials, contributing to the development of groundbreaking therapies with the potential to transform patient lives.

This role will require a minimum of 3 days a week of onsite presence (or more as business needs require) in either of our Jersey City (NJ) or Millbrae (CA) offices to ensure effective management, operational excellence and high-performance delivery of clinical studies and to support the expected significant team growth & collaboration.

About You

You are passionate about playing a key role in supporting the planning, coordination, and execution of clinical trials within the oncology portfolio. You have strong communication skills and a passion for advancing care to patients.

What You’ll Do

• Assist in the preparation and maintenance of essential study documents, including study protocols, informed consent forms, case report forms (CRFs), and other trial-related materials.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure accurate and timely completion of study start-up activities, such as site selection, feasibility assessments, and ethics committee submissions.

• Support the organization and conduct of investigator meetings, study initiation visits, and other trial-related meetings.

• Coordinate and track the distribution, collection, and reconciliation of trial supplies, investigational products, and study related materials.

• Assist in the review and resolution of data queries, ensuring data accuracy and completeness within electronic data capture (EDC) systems.

• In collaboration with TMF Operations team, maintain trial master files (TMFs) and study documentation in accordance with regulatory requirements and internal SOPs.

• Facilitate effective communication among study team members, investigators, and study site personnel through regular correspondence and timely dissemination of study-related information.

• Support the monitoring and tracking of study progress, including patient recruitment and enrollment, to ensure adherence to study timelines and milestones.

• In collaboration with other Clinical Operations groups (Site Engagement and Monitoring Excellence) assist, as necessary, in the preparation and coordination of site monitoring visits, ensuring compliance with monitoring plans and resolution of site-related issues.

• Stay updated with relevant regulations, guidelines, and industry best practices pertaining to oncology clinical trials, ensuring compliance, and implementing necessary changes as required.

Qualifications

• An Advanced Degree without experience or Bachelor's degree with 2 years of experience in a relevant field (e.g., life sciences, healthcare, or related discipline).

• Ability to communicate in multiple languages (especially European languages) will be considered a strong asset.

• Previous experience working as a Clinical Trials Associate, Study Coordinator, or in a similar role within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry is preferred.

• Knowledge of clinical trial regulations, guidelines, and best practices, including ICH-GCP and FDA requirements.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize workload effectively.

• Proficiency in using clinical trial management systems (CTMS) and electronic data capture (EDC) systems.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively interact with study team members and internal / external stakeholders.

• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team-oriented environment.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project).

• Adaptability and willingness to learn and embrace new technologies, processes, and industry trends.

At Eikon, employee compensation also includes bonus and equity compensation, in addition to several generous benefit programs, including:​

• 401k plan with company matching​

• Medical (premiums covered by Eikon at 95%), dental and vision insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%)​

• Mental health and wellness benefits​

• Weeklong summer and winter holiday shutdowns​

• Generous paid time off and holiday policies​

• Life/AD&D Insurance (premiums covered by Eikon at 100%) and optional supplemental employee-paid life/AD&D policies ​

• Enhanced parental leave benefit​

• Daily subsidized lunch program when on-site​

The expected salary range for this role is $104,000 to $126,000 depending on skills, competency, and the market demand for your expertise.

Eikon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment.

We are currently not accepting any new third-party agencies or firms at this time. Please do not forward unsolicited agency resumes to our website, employees or Human Resources. Eikon Therapeutics will not pay fees to any third-party agency or firm associated with unsolicited resumes.

• Implement process standardization and compliance, and create programs that encourage employee participation

• A.S. or B.S. in Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Industrial Engineering, or a related field

• 3–5 years of lab experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably in a supervisory or management role, plus 2+ years of Operational Excellence experience

• Lean Six Sigma certification (required for external applicants; preferred for internal applicants)

• Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment; biotech, pharma, or medical device experience strongly preferred

• Knowledge of quality management systems, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, and GMP

• Proven project management skills

• Ability to coach associates, leads, and supervisors

• Strong problem-solving and communication skills

• Innovative and motivated, with a proven ability to work cross-functionally and drive accountability

Twist Bioscience synthesizes genes from scratch, known as “writing” DNA. Just as children learn to both read and write, the next phase of development for the genomics revolution is the ability to write DNA.

At Twist Bioscience, we work in service of people who are changing the world for the better. jobs.description:
ABOUT AFTERQUERY

AfterQuery https://www.afterquery.com/ is an applied research lab curating data solutions for foundation model development. We serve every frontier AI lab with the mission of delivering the best data to power the best models. In doing so, we can make expertise that once took a lifetime to build available to anyone who needs it. 

Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We're based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI.




WHY APPLY

Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we're not slowing down.

Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up.

Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity, giving you a real stake in the company's success. Join at an early stage, grow alongside the business, and participate directly in the upside you help create. As we scale, so will your opportunities, responsibilities, and impact.

Strong Team: Work alongside world-class engineers, researchers, and operators.



About the role

This is our first strategic finance hire, reporting to the Head of Finance & Accounting. You will own planning, budgets and analytics, and build them AI-native from the start, so we run the business off the data and invest in what builds a durable business.

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to get into the weeds and build. You start as the only person in FP&A, building your own models, data and tools, and grow the team as the function grows. A prior Head of FP&A title is not required. We weigh what you have built over the titles you have held.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



Own the plan

 - Own the operating model, the annual plan and the monthly forecast.

 - Set targets and budgets, and help each team understand its headcount and expenses.

 - Build customer- and contract-level unit economics and forecast capacity.

 - Work with teams to optimize fixed and variable costs across experts, inference and compute.

 - Forecast compute and inference spend, and model capacity commitments before we sign them.

 - Own the cash forecast and quarterly tax estimates, so large payments are planned ahead.

Run the business off the data

 - Build the data layer from the ledger, CRM, payroll, spend and delivery systems.

 - Own the metric definitions and the quarterly business review.

 - Deliver budget-vs-actual and variance analysis each month.

 - Partner with Accounting so management reporting ties to the close every month.

Build with AI

 - Automate the planning and reporting cycle with AI and agentic workflows, with checks back to source.

 - Keep the business context encoded so the tools know the business at the start of every cycle.

Support decisions

 - Price new work, run deal reviews and model deal structure with the Delivery, Engagement and Operations teams.

 - Build the business case for new products and verticals before we commit people and spend.

 - Own board and investor materials, and support capital allocation decisions.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Models, data pipelines and AI workflows you built yourself that replaced manual FP&A work, with results you can quantify.

 - Hands-on SQL, Python, Claude Code or Codex experience. You pull your own data and run your own analysis.

 - Comfortable forecasting a business and industry that change quarter to quarter, and updating the assumptions when they do.

 - The judgment to know when an output is wrong.

 - A foundation in investment banking, consulting or strategic finance, and hands-on FP&A at a hyper-growth technology company.

 - You explain the numbers plainly to founders and engineers, and push back with data.

 - High ownership, low ego, and comfort with direct feedback.

 - Comfortable working five days a week in our San Francisco office.


BONUS

 - Building or running a planning process from scratch.

jobs.title: Director Clinical Quality and Compliance
jobs.description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

The Director of Clinical Quality & Compliance is responsible for the strategic oversight, management, and execution of clinical quality assurance and regulatory compliance programs across pre-market and post-market clinical research initiatives. The role will work closely with internal Clinical Operations teams and cross-functional partners to support and monitor compliance, ensure adherence with FDA IDE requirements and Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and maintain inspection readiness across all studies, both  internally managed  and externally initiated or managed.

Job Responsibilities:

• Leads clinical quality and regulatory compliance strategies and initiatives across pre-market and post-market internal and external clinical programs.

• Ensures robust end-to-end clinical trial compliance with FDA Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines (21 CFR Parts 50, 56, 312, 812) and ISO 14155.

• Oversees medical device labeling requirements, ensuring full compliance with FDA regulations and international labeling standards for post-market and investigational devices.

• Authors, reviews, and maintains Investigator’s Brochures (IB) for investigational medical devices being used in clinical research programs.

• Leads Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) audit preparation, internal GCP audits, vendor oversight, and external regulatory health authority inspections.

• Works closely with internal Clinical Operations and external CRO teams to ensure study protocols, execution strategies, and trial management practices align with regulatory and quality standards.

• Establishes clinical trial monitoring protocols and oversees key study deliverables, including Informed Consent Forms (ICFs), site monitoring oversight plans, and Trial Master File (TMF) quality standards.

• Partners with Clinical Operations to review regulatory document packages required for site greenlighting, ensuring ongoing Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee (EC) approvals, protocol amendments, and revised ICF implementations remain compliant across all sites.

• Manages regulatory compliance oversight for Unanticipated Adverse Device Effects (UADE) and Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reporting workflows, ensuring strict adherence to FDA 10-day reporting windows, IRB/EC notifications, and safety monitoring plans.

• Implements systematic oversight for logging, evaluating, and mitigating protocol deviations and non-compliance, ensuring thorough root-cause analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) in partnership with internal Clinical Operations.

• Partners with Clinical Operations to establish quality oversight and compliance metrics ensuring field monitors and study personnel execute the trial strictly per the approved protocol and Instructions for Use (IFU).

• Partners with Regulatory Affairs to ensure post-market regulatory obligations are met, including contribution and review of Clinical Evaluation Reports (CER), Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) studies, Literature Searches, and Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSUR).

• Contributes to FDA Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) regulatory strategies and submissions.

• Navigates geographic data governance, data privacy, and cross-border clinical regulatory requirements for multi-site global trials.

• Participates in and leads process improvement activities within the department and cross-functionally alongside Clinical Operations.

Skills Needed:

• Deep technical knowledge of FDA IDE regulations, FDA GCP standards, ISO 14155, and medical device labeling requirements.

• Strong experience partnering closely with internal Clinical Operations teams to ensure robust GCP compliance in study management processes.

• Direct hands-on experience hosting FDA BIMO audits and preparing sponsors/vendors for regulatory health authority inspections.

• Demonstrated expertise reviewing and managing ICFs, IBs, IFUs, PMCF plans, and PSUR compilation.

• Extensive background managing protocol deviations, CAPA systems, and UADE/SAE safety reporting within regulated clinical trials.

• Understanding of multi-geographic clinical trial execution, data integrity, and cross-border regulatory considerations.

• Strong matrix leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to drive cross-functional compliance.

• Incredible attention to detail, accuracy, and quality.

• Ability to manage multiple tasks and work comfortably in an environment with shifting priorities.

• Ability to work in a collaborative team environment with a willing, all-hands-on-deck attitude.

• Excellent written and oral English communication skills required.

• Proficiency in computer programs, specifically Microsoft Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Google tools.

Educational Requirements & Work Experience:

• Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Biomedical Engineering, Clinical Research, or related scientific/health field (Master's, Ph.D., PharmD, or RN preferred).

• Demonstrated minimum of 8 years relevant experience in clinical quality assurance and regulatory affairs within the medical device, biotech, or combination product industries.

• Demonstrated experience leading BIMO audit readiness and FDA IDE submissions preferred.

• Proven track record of working in close alignment with internal Clinical Operations teams.

• Experience managing CROs and clinical vendors required.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary compensation range is $215,000 to $240,000, bonus, and equity. #LI-Hybrid

We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at Heartflow, including recruitment, hiring, training, relocation, promotion, and termination.

Positions posted for Heartflow are not intended for or open to third party recruiters / agencies. Submission of any unsolicited resumes for these positions will be considered to be free referrals.

jobs.title: Senior Materials R&D Engineer, Composites
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.

Radiant is seeking a highly motivated Senior Materials R&D Engineer, Composites to support the development, optimization, and scale-up of advanced ceramic composite processes for the Kaleidos 1MW nuclear microreactor. This role will focus on transitioning lab-scale processes from research and development into safe, reliable, repeatable, and scalable production operations. You will work closely with materials engineers and technicians to mature processes including chemical vapor infiltration (CVI), filament winding, and ceramic joining. The ideal candidate has strong mechanical aptitude, hands-on experience with manufacturing equipment, and a passion for improving process capability through equipment design, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement. You will play a key role in establishing the manufacturing capabilities necessary to produce high-quality ceramic composite components for Radiant’s first commercial reactor.

Responsibilities & Duties

 - Develop, optimize, and qualify materials and manufacturing processes for ceramic composite components, including chemical vapor infiltration (CVI), filament winding, and ceramic joining.

 - Transition R&D processes into repeatable, controlled, and scalable manufacturing operations with an emphasis on process safety, part quality, reliability, and throughput.

 - Design, specify, and implement upgrades to manufacturing equipment and supporting systems, including vacuum pumps, valves, gas delivery systems, fixtures, and tooling.

 - Identify and resolve equipment and process limitations to improve process control, operational reliability, and manufacturing efficiency.

 - Develop process documentation, standard operating procedures, and work instructions to enable consistent execution by technicians.

 - Establish and monitor critical process parameters and metrics to evaluate process capability, identify variation, and drive continuous improvement.

 - Design and develop fixtures, tooling, and equipment modifications to improve component handling, process consistency, and production throughput.

 - Lead troubleshooting and root cause investigations of process deviations, equipment failures, and manufacturing defects.

 - Define process requirements, evaluate component quality, and implement improvements to manufacturing methods.

 - Support equipment installation, commissioning, preventative maintenance planning, and qualification of manufacturing processes.

 - Identify and implement improvements to manufacturing safety, equipment reliability, and operational efficiency.

Required Qualifications & Skills

 - Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

 - 5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, equipment engineering, or related technical roles.

 - Hands-on experience developing, operating, troubleshooting, or improving manufacturing equipment and processes.

 - Strong mechanical aptitude and understanding of industrial equipment, including mechanical systems, instrumentation, and process controls.

 - Experience designing or modifying mechanical components, fixtures, or tooling using CAD software.

 - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, mechanical schematics, and technical documentation.

 - Experience identifying root causes of equipment or manufacturing process issues and implementing corrective actions.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an ability to apply engineering principles to practical manufacturing challenges.

 - Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills.

 - Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with engineering and operations teams in a hands-on manufacturing environment.

Desired Qualifications & Skills

 - Experience with ceramic matrix composites (CMCs), technical ceramics, or other advanced materials manufacturing processes.

 - Experience with chemical vapor infiltration (CVI), chemical vapor deposition (CVD), filament winding, or high-temperature ceramic joining processes.

 - Experience designing, operating, or maintaining high-temperature vacuum furnaces, pressure vessels, autoclaves, or similar processing equipment.

 - Knowledge of vacuum technology, pumps, valves, gas delivery systems, pressure instrumentation, and process control equipment.

 - Experience with manufacturing processes involving hazardous gases, elevated temperatures, or vacuum and pressure systems.

 - Familiarity with process automation, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), and data acquisition systems.

 - Experience with manufacturing process qualification, statistical process control (SPC), design of experiments (DOE), and process capability analysis.

 - Experience applying design for manufacturability (DFM), lean manufacturing, and continuous improvement principles.

 - Experience developing manufacturing processes and equipment for transition from prototype to production.

 - Experience with materials characterization, inspection techniques, and quality control methods for advanced materials.

Additional Requirements

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must work 100% onsite in El Segundo, CA.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Bills
jobs.description:
Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is building the payment layer for life's financial obligations, giving households one place to see, split, and pay their bills around how they live and get paid. By offering greater choice over how and when payments are made and allowing eligible on time payments to help build a positive credit history, Flex puts households back in control of their cash flow.

That work brings together people with different perspectives who challenge the status quo and take ownership of solving difficult problems. For you, that means doing the best work of your career next to people who make you better, and together bringing ideas to life that make a real impact for the people we serve.

About the role

Flex is looking for a Principal Product Manager, Bills to guide how returning users go from paying one bill with Flex to paying many. They are responsible for setting the strategy for our cross-sell and upsell experiences and taking responsibility for making our existing user base a durable, profitable source of growth.

The right person sees the business as funnels and systems, weighs the user experience against unit economics and credit risk, and builds growth through the product itself. Your work will span our app and web surfaces, from how users find and add bills to how we personalize what they see next, and you will help shape new ways for Flex to create value for users and for the billers we work with.

What you'll do

• Set the direction for cross-sell and upsell. Define the strategy and a staged roadmap that carries returning users from their first bill on Flex to the next one.

• Grow adoption through the product. Lead the app and web experiences that turn existing users into multi-bill users, and be accountable for cross-sell rate, cross-sold users, and bills per user.

• Make bills easy to find and add. Shape bill discovery, bill management, and multi-bill experiences.

• Personalize what comes next. Decide the best next action for each user, and run the experiments that show whether it works.

• Explore new monetization. Work out how billers and offers should appear to users while protecting user trust and credit risk.

• Team up with Marketing and Analytics on lifecycle programs, measurement, and holdout tests.

• Align the people around you. Earn buy-in from Engineering, Design, Risk, Compliance, Finance, and Revenue without relying on formal authority, and keep decisions moving.

• Raise the bar for the craft. Mentor other PMs, write clearly about hard problems, and help Bills scale our product development processes.

Key qualifications

• At least 7 years of product management experience, with demonstrable impact owning growth, monetization, or lifecycle products at a consumer or B2B2C fintech, marketplace, or subscription business.

• Growth beyond launch. You have taken a product from one to sixty, scaling it past its initial launch while still validating what works. You have moved existing users to broader adoption, and you can tell activation, adoption, and truly incremental lift apart.

• Systems thinker with a track record of turning ambiguous spaces into staged roadmaps and operating cadences, and spotting interdependencies with risk, credit, and money movement.

• Analytical horsepower: fluency in SQL and BI tools such as Sigma, comfort modeling unit economics and payback, and rigor in experiment design.

jobs.title: Senior Named Account Sales Director, AI & Enterprise
jobs.description:
The weaponization of AI is driving a paradigm shift in the cyber security industry from proactive to preemptive security:  clients must now invest more intelligence and effort in understanding their vulnerabilities before their adversaries do (Open AI).  The only way to achieve this is to simulate future attack scenarios at scale, and to run them in high fidelity digital replicas of production environments (Gartner/Forrester).  SimSpace serves as the AI Proving Grounds to generate hypersynthetic data which pressure tests controls, tools, teams, and agentic capabilities in full kill chain attacks hidden in realistic environmental traffic and patterns of life. 



Founded in 2015 by experts from U.S. Cyber Command and MIT Lincoln Laboratory, the platform was initially conceived to assist in Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO), to quickly replicate target environments to conduct mission rehearsal of human operators and their tools to deny (disrupt, degrade, destroy) or deceive (manipulate or exfiltrate data) adversaries.  The company has since expanded to serve over a dozen allied governments in OCO/DCO as well as critical infrastructure enterprises around the world.  The company is actively investing in the Americas, Asia Pacific, Europe and the Middle East through direct sales and channel partners.  SimSpace has launched the AI Proving Grounds Consortium, leading the revolution by creating an open platform for the InfoSec ecosystem to train, validate and operationalize their agentic capabilities before committing to production.



Why join SimSpace?

We are a team united by a shared purpose and four core values: Serve to Protect, Acquire Understanding, Teamwork without Borders, and Operate as Innovators. We value candid, constructive feedback and create opportunities for personal, professional, and financial growth. Our vision, “Defend the Free World,” drives our mission: “Defeat Any Adversary in Any Cyber Terrain at Machine Speed.”



How Do We Work?

We listen to customers and colleagues, challenge assumptions, and turn ideas into meaningful results. We expect everyone to embrace emerging technologies, simplify and automate work, and use AI to learn, solve problems, and help deliver quality with speed. We apply human judgment and take responsibility for outcomes. Whether remote or office-based, we collaborate across teams and time zones.



We invite you to apply today!




THE OPPORTUNITY

SimSpace is building the AI Proving Grounds: a destructive-safe, non-production environment where organizations evaluate AI agents, tools, teams, and processes before deployment—and continue testing as they evolve.



We’re hiring a high-ownership enterprise seller to lead a small portfolio of strategic AI providers and selected AI-leading enterprises. You will work directly with security, AI, and executive teams to identify consequential use cases, shape evaluations around customer outcomes, and carry opportunities from first conversation through close and expansion.



This role calls for deep account focus, technical curiosity, and strong commercial judgment. You’ll spend your time building executive access and advancing a small number of important accounts.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a deliberately small portfolio—approximately 5–8 named accounts—with tailored account plans, stakeholder maps, and clear next steps.

 - Engage in model building, evaluation and hill-climbing activities alongside strategic model providers

 - Build relationships with CISOs and security leaders, AI and engineering leaders, and the management budget owners who can fund the work.

 - Lead direct, account-specific outreach and develop credible introduction paths through customers, executives, and partners.

 - Learn how each account is developing and deploying AI agents; identify where security teams need evidence before agents or workflows move into production.

 - Turn customer priorities into specific evaluation use cases, such as testing agent behavior, security workflows, tools, and teams against realistic adversarial scenarios.

 - Work with Sales Engineering, Field CISO, Product, and Professional Services to shape the right technical and commercial approach.

 - Lead structured what-if workshops that surface current, consequential problems and produce written value hypotheses with the right customer stakeholders.

 - Recommend a Proof of Value only when the management budget owner is engaged, success criteria are agreed, and the decision and procurement paths are understood.

 - Lead negotiations, security and legal reviews, procurement, and contracting through to a signed agreement.

 - Protect full-value positioning and keep the forecast grounded in customer evidence, buying commitments, and a clear path to a decision.

 - Ensure a clean transition to Customer Success, support customer outcomes, and identify opportunities for expansion while remaining primary account owner before, during and after closed-won

 - Bring structured customer feedback to Product and company leadership without making unsupported roadmap commitments.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Each assigned account has an actionable plan, a current stakeholder map, and a clear view of its AI initiatives, security priorities, budget ownership, and decision path.

 - Customer conversations progress from general interest to a validated use case with an accountable owner and a fundable initiative.

 - Workshops end with written value hypotheses and an agreed next step—or a clear decision to stop pursuing the opportunity.

 - Proofs of Value have customer-agreed success criteria, an engaged budget owner, a defined timebox, and a scheduled decision meeting.

 - You create and close meaningful enterprise revenue while maintaining forecast accuracy and pricing discipline.

 - Customers adopt the capability and can describe the operational value it provides.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 7+ years of full-cycle enterprise sales experience, with a track record of personally creating and closing complex technical opportunities.

 - Experience selling cybersecurity, AI infrastructure, cloud, developer platforms, or similarly technical solutions to large organizations.

 - Strong executive presence with the ability to engage CISOs, technology leaders, AI teams, and economic buyers.

 - Skill in account planning, executive outreach, multi-threading, discovery, value development, negotiation, and contracting.

 - The ability to translate technical and operational detail into a clear business case and buying decision.

 - Comfort working with technical teams to understand customer environments, use cases, evaluation needs, and deployment constraints.

 - A disciplined approach to qualification: you can distinguish a current, owned, fundable problem from curiosity or general interest.

 - Experience operating independently in an early-stage or high-growth company, where priorities move quickly and good judgment matters.

 - Curiosity about AI agents, cybersecurity, adversarial testing, security operations, and how organizations evaluate new technology.

 - A collaborative, low-ego working style and a reputation for following through.




HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

 - Selling to strategic AI providers, AI labs, hyperscalers, or Fortune 100 technology and enterprise organizations.

 - Working with AI evaluation, AI security, red teaming, purple teaming, SOC modernization, cyber operations, or simulation.

 - Building executive relationships through partners, customer referrals, or an established network in AI or cybersecurity.




LOCATION

Must be based in the Western United States and able to travel for customer and company meetings.



WE’RE PROUD TO OFFER A COMPETITIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE PACKAGE DESIGNED TO SUPPORT YOUR WELL-BEING, GROWTH, AND SUCCESS:

 - Compensation. Base salary range: $200,000 - $220,000 reflecting our confidence in your expertise and impact, with the opportunity for commission tied to company performance and individual contributions.

 - Health & Wellness. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits, plus savings plans—coverage starts on day one!

 - Mental Health Support. Access to company-paid counseling, coaching, and resources for you and your family through Spring Health.

 - Financial Well-Being. Plan for your future with a 401(k)-retirement savings plan featuring a company match.

 - Flexible Time Off. Take the time you need with unlimited vacation and dedicated health & wellness days. SimSpace provides flexible solutions to meet the diverse work-life needs of team members.

jobs.title: Director, Wholesale
jobs.description:
Director, Wholesale

Department: Wholesale

Reports to: VP, Retail and Wholesale

Employment Type: Full Time

Location: Remote (United States) or NYC (preferred)

Pay Range: $150k-$160k annually

About Margaux

Margaux is a modern footwear brand rooted in duality, inspired by the ideas that style and comfort can coexist, that softness and structure aren’t mutually exclusive, and that everyday style translates for the big moments, too. Co-founders Sarah Pierson and Alexa Buckley Roussel launched Margaux in 2015, setting out to create a footwear wardrobe for women on the go, powered by thoughtful design and an innovative approach to construction. The collection began with a classic ballet flat and has since grown into a full range of silhouettes. Each pair of Margaux shoes is designed in New York City, handmade in Spain, and thoughtfully crafted to withstand the test of time. Margaux is based in downtown New York City, with a satellite office in San Francisco and a team at our family-owned factory in southern Spain. For more about the brand, visit us online.

The role

Margaux is growing its wholesale business across marketplace, dropship, traditional and U.S. department store partners, and we’re looking for a Director of Wholesale to lead it. You’ll be the primary point of contact for our department store partners, the person buyers and merchants call first. You’ll also run wholesale like a business: you own the P&L, set strategy across channels, and know the numbers behind every decision. Our first U.S. department store rollout sits at the center of the plan. You’ll partner closely with our Senior Director of Merchandising on line planning, and with our Senior Manager of Wholesale and Operations, who own forecasting, allocation, reporting, order administration, fulfillment and retailer compliance.

What you'll do

• Be the primary point of contact for executive, buyer and merchant relationships at our department store, marketplace and international partners.

• Lead our department store rollout: door selection, the pace of adding doors, and a business case for each door.

• Run seasonal business reviews with each partner on sell-through, door productivity and growth plans.

• Find, pitch and onboard new accounts, including international and luxury partners, and lead brand presentations to new and existing partners.

• Lead line planning for each account with Merchandising: category, depth and price tiers.

• Lead market and line-review meetings, sell-in, assortment negotiation and buy commitments, through delivery and sell-through.

• Set brand presentation standards on partner floors and training priorities for partner staff.

• Own the wholesale P&L, annual budget and revenue targets, partnering with Finance and managing to weekly sales against plan.

• Grow profitability by managing stock turn, margin, markdowns and returns.

• Negotiate commercial terms: vendor agreements, margin and fee structures, co-op, markdown allowances and returns to vendor (RTVs).

• Manage the wholesale marketing and co-op budget, with clear accountability for return on spend.

• Set channel strategy across marketplace, dropship, department store and traditional wholesale, consistent with our own ecommerce and stores on price and brand.

What you bring

• 10+ years in wholesale, sales or account management for a fashion, footwear or accessories brand, including 5+ in a senior, account-facing role.

• Experience as the primary point of contact for a major U.S. department store, including a multi-door rollout, ideally in a category with many SKUs like footwear.

• Real commercial and financial depth: you’ve owned a P&L and budget and can walk through one line by line. A background in business operations, strategy, consulting or a general manager role is a strong plus.

• Hands-on experience across dropship, marketplace, ecommerce and department store channels, and a point of view on how they fit together.

• A track record of launching or scaling a wholesale channel and opening new accounts.

• Experience with line planning, negotiating commercial terms, and managing a co-op budget to ROI.

• You’re as comfortable in a spreadsheet as in a buyer meeting, fluent in sell-through, stock turn and door productivity.

• A builder’s mindset: you turn plans into results, question what you’re told (including AI output), and pick up new tools quickly.

• Executive presence, with the credibility to represent Margaux to partner leadership.

What We Offer

• Competitive compensation commensurate with experience

• Comprehensive benefits for eligible roles, which may include medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, and paid time off

• Paid sick leave

• Employee discount on all Margaux products

• A close-knit, mission-driven team culture

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Technician, Ceramic Composites
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.

Radiant is seeking a Senior Engineering Technician to support the fabrication and processing of advanced ceramic composite components for our development microreactor unit. This role will be responsible for operating and maintaining high-temperature vacuum furnaces and associated process equipment, preparing components for processing, and ensuring that manufacturing operations are performed safely, consistently, and in accordance with engineering instructions. You will work closely with materials and manufacturing engineers to execute production processes, monitor equipment performance, and troubleshoot issues as they arise. As a foundational member of the materials processing team, you will play a key role in maintaining a clean, organized, and efficient manufacturing environment with a strong emphasis on 5S principles, equipment reliability, and operational excellence.

Responsibilities and Duties:

 - Operate high-temperature vacuum furnaces and associated processing equipment in accordance with engineering-provided process instructions.

 - Prepare ceramic composite components for processing, including material handling, cleaning, fixturing, loading, and unloading of furnaces.

 - Perform dimensional inspections, weight measurements, and visual inspections of components before and after processing.

 - Monitor processing operations, including temperature, pressure, gas flow, and other process parameters, to ensure compliance with established process instructions.

 - Accurately document process conditions, equipment performance, inspection results, and any deviations from established procedures.

 - Perform routine equipment maintenance, cleaning, and preventative maintenance to ensure reliable operation of furnaces and supporting equipment.

 - Troubleshoot and repair mechanical, electrical, vacuum, and other equipment issues in collaboration with engineering.

 - Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work environment through consistent application of 5S principles and established housekeeping standards.

 - Partner and collaborate with engineers to identify equipment issues, improve manufacturing workflows, and support process improvements.

 - Abide by a high level of operational standards regarding safety, reliability, cleanliness, and quality.

 - Perform other tasks as needed. We are a small company, and you may need to perform tasks outside your normal duties and responsibilities.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

 - High school diploma or equivalent certificate.

 - 3+ years of experience in a manufacturing, fabrication, equipment operation, or technician role.

 - Strong mechanical aptitude and ability to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair industrial equipment.

 - Ability to follow detailed written process instructions and accurately document manufacturing operations.

 - Strong attention to detail, organization, and commitment to maintaining a clean and orderly workspace.

 - Experience using basic hand tools, power tools, and traditional inspection equipment.

 - Ability to perform dimensional measurements using calipers, micrometers, and other inspection tools.

 - Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings and basic equipment schematics.

 - Positive attitude and ability to work effectively as part of a team.

 - Ability to work independently and efficiently with minimal supervision.

 - Ability to recognize abnormal equipment behavior and promptly communicate issues to engineering.

 - Physical effort including standing, lifting, and carrying equipment up to 50 lbs. unassisted.

Desired Skills and Qualifications:

 - Experience operating vacuum furnaces, tube furnaces, autoclaves, or other high-temperature or pressure-processing equipment.

 - Experience working with vacuum systems, pumps, pressure controls, gas delivery systems, and associated instrumentation.

 - Experience with ceramic materials, composite materials, or other advanced materials manufacturing processes.

 - Experience performing preventative maintenance and troubleshooting industrial processing equipment.

 - Familiarity with thermocouples, temperature controllers, pressure gauges, mass flow controllers, and other process instrumentation.

 - Experience performing leak checks and troubleshooting vacuum or pressurized systems.

 - Familiarity with 5S, lean manufacturing principles, and manufacturing housekeeping standards.

 - Experience operating safely in industrial or laboratory manufacturing environments.

 - Proficient computer skills; comfortable using email, Microsoft Office, and electronic process documentation systems.

Additional Requirements:

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to achieve company goals.

 - Must work 100% onsite at El Segundo HQ.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

jobs.title: Facility Security Officer (FSO)
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team

As Facility Security Officer (FSO), you will serve as Relativity's designated FSO and lead the build-out of our industrial security program as we upgrade our Facility Clearance (FCL). You'll own day-to-day facility clearance administration, DD254 management, and SCIF accreditation efforts, serving as a primary point of contact with DCSA, while partnering closely with the Director of Physical Security on broader enterprise security initiatives. This is a hands-on, build-focused role for someone who wants to stand up a TS/SCI security program, not simply maintain one that's already in place.

About the Role

• Serve as Relativity's designated Facility Security Officer (FSO) with active TS/SCI clearance, owning all facility clearance (FCL) requirements, DD254 management, and serving as primary interface with DCSA and government security agencies for classified program compliance.

• Lead the build-out and upgrade of Relativity's Facility Clearance from Secret to TS/SCI, including sponsorship and upgrade request coordination, KMP and organizational structure documentation, and all associated DCSA submission requirements.

• Own SCIF accreditation efforts in accordance with ICD 705, including construction security plan (CSP) input, physical and technical security requirements, and development and submission of the accreditation package.

• Administer and mature NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117) compliance programs, including personnel security processing for TS/SCI access, visitor control, classified information handling, self-inspections, and insider threat program support.

• Maintain continuous audit readiness for DCSA and government security agency reviews, including documentation, training records, and corrective action tracking.

• Partner with the Director of Physical Security, Legal, People, and Facilities teams to align personnel actions, construction projects, and program security requirements with FCL and SCIF accreditation milestones.

About You

• Active TS/SCI security clearance and current FSO certification, with demonstrated experience administering facility clearances and interfacing with DCSA and government security agencies.

• 5+ years of progressive industrial/physical security experience, including at least 2 years serving as a Facility Security Officer; direct experience supporting a Secret-to-TS/SCI FCL upgrade or SCIF accreditation effort is strongly preferred.

• Working knowledge of NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117), ICD 705, and classified program security requirements, with experience supporting successful government audits and regulatory compliance.

• Familiarity with security systems technologies (e.g., access control, CCTV/VMS, intrusion detection) sufficient to support accreditation and compliance requirements.

• Strong attention to detail and documentation discipline, with the ability to manage complex regulatory submissions and multiple concurrent compliance workstreams.

• Ability to communicate security and compliance requirements clearly to non-technical stakeholders across the organization.

Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP

Provide direct leadership and operational oversight for the distribution center, ensuring consistent processes, throughput, standards, and performance across sites.

Own execution of daily, weekly, and monthly operating plans for receiving, put‑away, storage, picking, loading, and dispatch.

Ensure adequate coverage and leadership presence for 24/7 operation, including nights and weekends, through effective scheduling and delegation.

PEOPLE LEADERSHIP & TEAM DEVELOPMENT

Lead, coach, and develop warehouse leadership teams.

Review and evaluate performance of all distribution center functions and direct reports, addressing performance gaps, and taking corrective action to ensure the managers of each functional area are delivering on operating goals.

Set clear expectations, conduct regular performance check‑ins, and support annual performance review processes.

Partner with HR on recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management, and employee relations matters.

Build a culture of accountability, respect, inclusion, and continuous improvement.

Conduct regular safety walks, audits, and incident reviews; ensure corrective actions are implemented and tracked.

Ensure facilities and equipment are maintained to company standards (housekeeping, MHE, racking, dock doors, yard, etc.).

SERVICE, QUALITY & INVENTORY CONTROL

Monitor and improve picking accuracy, damage rates, load quality, and adherence to standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Assist the General Manager with acting as the local liaison for internal partners.

Manage labor planning, staffing levels, and shift structures to match volume while controlling overtime and temporary labor usage.

Track and report key performance indicators (KPIs) for both facilities (safety, quality, productivity, throughput, cost per case, overall service).

BUSINESS CONTINUITY & 24/7 READINESS

7+ years of progressive experience in warehouse/distribution center operations; at least 4 years in a leadership role (multi‑shift or multi‑site preferred).

Proven track record of managing and developing front‑line teams and supervisors.

Strong knowledge of warehouse operations, WMS systems, inventory control, and safety practices.

Ability to work flexibly in support of 24/7 operations (evenings, nights, weekends, and on‑call as needed).

Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and decision‑making skills; comfortable working with KPIs and data.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; able to influence across different functions and levels.
