jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Join Axon and be a Force for Good

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues through devices and cloud software. Life here is fast-paced, challenging, and meaningful. You’ll take ownership, grow constantly, and help build products that matter—for a mission that matters.

Your Impact

As an L9 Senior Technical Program Manager II, you will raise the execution bar for how we build software across DEMS. You will own two systemic problems: making project status rigorous and actionable, and turning project maturity into data we use to decide where engineering time goes. You will work as an autonomous, cross-team leader, using AI tools as leverage to coach teams. You won’t do the work for them.

Today, status updates are mostly written by software engineers or their AI agents. They describe activity, but they rarely say what changed against the plan, what is at risk, or what decision is needed. At the same time, we start projects at very different levels of readiness and have no consistent way to see that before we commit engineers. You will build the mechanism that fixes both: in effect, an AI reviewer for Execution Reviews. It checks the tactics (is this status honest, specific, and actionable?) and the strategy (is this project mature enough to deserve the engineering time we’re spending on it?). It starts in one Software Engineering org and is meant to scale across DEMS.

What You’ll Do

Location: Scottsdale, AZ

Reports to: Director, Software Engineering

Direct Reports: None (individual contributor role)

Execution Rigor & Status Reporting

• Define the bar for a good status update: progress against plan and dates, confidence, risks with owners and mitigations, and the decisions or help needed, from whom, and by when.

• Build and tune AI-assisted reviewers that grade status updates against that bar and give feedback to the author before the update goes out, whether a human or an agent wrote it.

• Coach engineers, tech leads, and engineering managers to write and run better status. Use the AI tooling to scale that coaching, not to replace it.

• Own program status reporting for the org and support rollups, MBRs, and portfolio reporting up to VP and SVP audiences.

Project Maturity & Portfolio Health

• Operationalize a Project Maturity Matrix that scores every active project across known dimensions: problem and customer validation, success criteria and metrics, technical approach, effort estimate, dependencies and ownership, investment justification, and kill criteria.

• Use AI to baseline projects from their real artifacts (docs, designs, plans, Jira), then track how each project matures over time. Require evidence: if there is no artifact, the project doesn’t get the score.

• Build the portfolio dataset by snapshotting scores every quarter and recording outcomes. Then answer the hard questions: Which dimensions actually predict success or slips? Where should we gate or throttle engineering investment until a project is ready?

• Bring data-backed recommendations to engineering and product leadership on where to invest, where to wait, and what evidence would move a project forward.

Stakeholder Alignment & Technical Decision Facilitation

• Hold your own in design and architecture reviews. Pressure-test estimates, dependencies, and trade-offs in data models, storage choices, APIs, scaling, and reliability.

• Work across teams and pillars when requirements contradict each other or are missing. Drive consensus, and escalate up to three levels with a clear recommendation (for example, a 1:3:1).

• Partner with engineering managers, product managers, and staff engineers so that program mechanisms help teams move faster instead of adding overhead.

Impact, Influence & Change Leadership

• Change habits across teams that don’t report to you. Make good execution hygiene the easy default.

• Create standard TPM artifacts (templates, rubrics, prompts, dashboards) that other teams and pillars adopt.

• Measure your own impact: better status quality, earlier risk detection, better project maturity at kickoff, and less engineering time spent on projects that weren’t ready.

Team Growth & Culture

• Mentor TPMs, engineering managers, and engineers on planning, status, risk framing, and looking around corners.

• Give talks and run working sessions on execution practices and on using AI tools well in the software development lifecycle.

• Interview senior TPMs and help raise the TPM bar across DEMS.

What You Bring

• 6–9+ years leading software programs from planning to delivery, including programs across multiple teams or pillars with ambiguous, contradictory, or missing requirements.

• Real technical depth. You understand system design, data flow, and data storage well enough to judge trade-offs: SQL vs. NoSQL, caching, where business logic lives, consistency vs. scale. You can explain those trade-offs clearly to engineers and to senior leaders.

• Fluency with data. You define metrics, build a dataset, separate signal from noise, and turn portfolio data into decisions instead of dashboards nobody reads.

• Hands-on experience with AI tools in your own work (LLMs, agents, prompt and workflow design), and good judgment about where they help and where they produce confident noise.

• Exceptional written communication. Your own status updates and docs are the example others copy.

• A track record of building mechanisms that outlast you, and of coaching people into better habits instead of policing them.

• Comfort presenting status, strategy, and recommendations up to SVP level, with candor and data.

• Command of multiple delivery methods (Scrum, Kanban, and others) and the judgment to pick the right one for the situation.

• Deep alignment with Axon’s values: you Aim Far with a long-term view, Own outcomes end-to-end, Expect Candor in communication, Win Right through principled execution, and Join Forces to scale impact.

• [Strongly Desired] 2–3+ years as a hands-on software engineer or other technical individual contributor.

• [Desired] Engineering or science degree, or equivalent experience.

Benefits that Benefit You

• Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Medical, Dental, Vision plans

• Fitness Programs

• Emotional & Mental Wellness support

• Learning & Development programs

• Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)

• And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.

For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.

All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. jobs.title: Clinical Genomics Scientist, Prenatal (Part-Time Contractor)
jobs.description:
A Rare Opportunity to Shape the Future of Genomics

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

BillionToOne is seeking an experienced Clinical Genomics Scientist to support variant curation and data analysis for our prenatal laboratory. You’ll classify germline variants for carrier screening and collaborate with our laboratory and clinical teams to ensure accurate, timely reporting.

This is a remote, part-time contract position of up to 20 hours per week.

Responsibilities:

• Curate and classify newly identified germline variants following ACMG/AMP/ClinGen guidelines.

• Reassess previously classified variants as new evidence emerges.

• Review scientific literature, human mutation databases, functional annotation resources, and genomic browsers (e.g., ClinVar, gnomAD, HGMD, UCSC Genome Browser, IGV) to support accurate classification and reporting.

• Meet turnaround targets while maintaining accuracy and thorough documentation.

Qualifications:

• Ph.D. in Human Genetics or a closely related field (other advanced degrees with relevant experience will be considered).

• 2+ years of experience in germline variant curation.

• Working knowledge of ACMG/AMP/ClinGen variant classification guidelines.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Demonstrated ability to classify variants efficiently within tight turnaround times.

• Strong preference for candidates with experience curating variants for carrier screening panels.

Benefits And Perks:

• Working alongside brilliant, kind, passionate and dedicated colleagues, in an empowering environment, toward a global vision, striving for a future in which transformative molecular diagnostics can help millions of patients

• The ability to indirectly or directly change the lives of hundreds of thousands patients

For this position, the target hourly rate is: $67 per hour.

BillionToOne is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

For more information about how we protect your information, we encourage you to review our Privacy Policy.

BillionToOne is a next-generation molecular diagnostics company on a mission to make powerful, accurate diagnostic tests accessible to everyone. Our revolutionary QCT molecular counting technology enhances disease detection resolution by over a thousandfold using cell-free DNA,a breakthrough that has already transformed the lives of over half a million patients worldwide.

Our Impact

Unity Complete™ is the only non-invasive prenatal screen capable of assessing fetal risk for both common recessive conditions and aneuploidies from a single maternal blood sample.
Unity Confirm™ enables non-invasive confirmation for high-risk screening results through the capture of intact circulating fetal cells using BillionToOne’s Fetal Cell Capture™ Technology.
Our Northstar® liquid biopsy test uniquely combines treatment selection with real-time monitoring, giving oncologists unprecedented precision in cancer care.

Our Growth

From $0 to $400M+ annualized revenue run-rate in just 6 years. In 2025, we completed one of the most successful IPOs for a medical diagnostics company, building on nearly $400M in private funding,including our $130M Series D in 2024 and backed by world-class investors including Hummingbird, Adams Street Partners, Neuberger Berman, Baillie Gifford, and Premji Invest.

Our Recognition

Forbes named us one of America's Best Startup Employers for 2025 and we're Great Place to Work certified, with 100% of our people willing to go the extra mile, even as we've scaled to over 700 employees.

Our Future

Headquartered in Menlo Park with facilities in Union City, CA, and a new lab opening in Austin, TX in 2027, we're continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible in molecular diagnostics. We're just getting started.

Ready to help us change the world, one molecule at a time? Learn more at billiontoone.com

jobs.title: International Field Operations Executive
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sieve is a multimodal data lab building high-quality training datasets and evaluation environments for frontier AI across audiovisual modeling, robotics, and multimodal interaction. We pair exabyte-scale data infrastructure and global data collection operations with multimodal research to help machines learn how the world looks, sounds, moves, and responds. Our work spans real and virtual environments, from large-scale video and audio to human demonstrations and evaluations of reasoning and action. We believe data creation deserves the same rigor as model development, and that a close connection between data production, model training, and evaluation is essential to building AI that can understand and interact with the world.

We partner with top AI labs and did $XXM last quarter alone, as a team of ~45 people. We also raised our Series A from Tier 1 firms such as Matrix Partners https://matrix.vc/, Swift Ventures https://www.swift.vc/, Y Combinator https://www.ycombinator.com/, and AI Grant https://aigrant.com/.



WHY NOW

Building the next generation of AI requires capturing data from the real world. We're expanding our hardware deployments across countries and need engineers who can get on the ground, figure things out, and make new sites work. You'll join early, own problems end-to-end, and help build the technical foundation for our international operations.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll run daily camera deployments at our recording sites in and around Bengaluru, and be the face of Sieve to the workers and site managers there. You'll report to Founding Operations, in the respective country. We'll provide hardware, training, and a playbook for each site.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Collect consent: Explain what we record, why, and how it's used, in the worker's language, and get signed or recorded consent before anyone wears a camera.

 - Deploy cameras: Fit cameras at the start of each shift, confirm they're recording, and collect them at the end.

 - Keep cameras running: Check every camera and wearer every 30 minutes and fix issues as they come up.

 - Look after workers: Answer questions honestly and help workers feel at ease.

 - Handle hardware and footage: Charge, label, and track devices, offload footage daily, and flag damaged or missing equipment.

 - Report daily: Log cameras deployed, hours recorded, and issues.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Every worker on camera has given informed consent, with complete records.

 - Every camera is mounted, recording, and accounted for through the full shift.

 - Workers keep participating and site managers are happy to keep hosting us.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Comfortable explaining consent and privacy in simple terms.

 - Able to track many devices and people at once.

 - Proactive, with a habit of regular follow-up.

 - Comfortable with basic hardware: charging, mounting, troubleshooting.

 - Kannada or Hindi, plus working English.

 - Willing to work full shifts on site and travel around Bengaluru.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with wearables, cameras, or field hardware.

 - Experience at a company collecting video or AI training data.

 - Experience in a factory, kitchen, warehouse, or shop-floor environment.

jobs.title: Intern, Automotive Interior Design, Summer 2027
jobs.description:

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. The Interior Design team defines and develops Lucid vehicle interiors, creating distinctive, human-centered environments that combine emotional design, intelligent functionality, craftsmanship, and progressive technology. The intern will contribute to active and future-facing vehicle programs through design research, concept development, sketching, digital visualization, design refinement, and presentation preparation. This internship is intended for an exceptionally capable design student who can contribute meaningfully, and will be expected to bring an original perspective, strong individual taste, and a point of view that expands the creative range of the team.

Role and Responsibilities

• Develop interior design concepts through research, storytelling, sketching, digital visualization, and iterative refinement

• Support future vehicle interiors, components, and user experiences

• Create mood boards, visual narratives, design proposals, and professional presentations

• Collaborate with Interior Design, Digital Modeling, CMF, UX/UI, Engineering, and other cross-functional partners

• Participate in design reviews and respond constructively to feedback

• Clearly communicate the customer relevance, emotional value, and design intent behind proposals

• Complete a defined body of work for an end-of-internship presentation

Must Have Skills

• Portfolio required. Applications cannot be evaluated without a portfolio

• Strong foundation in automotive interior, transportation, industrial, or product design

• Excellent drawing, sketching, and visual communication

• Understanding of proportion, form, composition, ergonomics, user experience, and three-dimensional space

• Ability to develop a concept from research through refinement and presentation

jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

This position has the opportunity to make a direct impact to Intuitive US marketing initiatives that deliver da Vinci Surgery to

patients worldwide. With the direction and guidance of the US Clinical Marketing leaders, you will develop, drive, and support the

US marketing efforts for Colorectal & Thoracic Surgery. You will have a particular focus on Colorectal & Thoracic Multi-Port &

Single Port procedures with the use of the da Vinci Surgical System and its associated products (e.g. Vessel Sealer Extend, Force

Bipolar etc.).

Essential Job Duties

This position will be responsible for development and coordination of various strategic and tactical clinical marketing initiatives to

drive procedure growth within the US Colorectal & Thoracic business. The individual will be expected to establish strong

relationships with the marketing and sales teams, external Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), as well as internal ISI stakeholders such

as other marketing departments, training, clinical affairs, legal, regulatory, and Market Access / Health Economics.

Build & execute high impact marketing plans and corresponding tactical plans / programs to achieve budgeted growth

projections in key areas of General Surgery.

 Develop qualitative and quantitative data and experiences to segment and deeply understand existing and new

markets, the surgeon, their practice, the patient journey, and the clinical procedure steps.

 Utilize market knowledge to design and develop strategies and value messaging (clinical, economic, operational,

strategic), collateral, tactics, and programs with demonstrated ROI.

 Assimilate Colorectal & Thoracic market trends and their potential implications to current and future

work/projects. Understand competition and develop competitive differentiation.

 Contribute to budget, resource allocation and financial planning for projects / programs with measured ROI to justify

through multiple marketing / media channels (webinars, sales collateral, etc.)

 Work with Key Opinion Leader surgeons to better understand how the da Vinci Surgical System and instruments are

being utilized and determine how to communicate that value proposition to other physicians.

 Develop and build KOLs by market segment with the goal of making Intuitive the preferred industry collaborator.

seen as an integral collaborator when planning congresses and implementing guidelines.

evaluate results and provide recommendations for future marketing promotions.

(clinical, hospital, or academic).

 Lead cross-functional teams to deliver high value marketing projects and programs.

approved claims, surgeon feedback, and sales input to maximize Intuitive’s footprint and growth trajectory in this area.

 Be a champion of the Intuitive culture; learning and embodying the company’s individual expectations for success.

jobs.description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The role:

SoFi is looking for a strategic, data-driven, and highly effective operator to join our Member Business Unit as Business Operations Director and Chief of Staff to the Member Executive Vice President. The Member team includes a diverse set of businesses and capabilities, including SoFi Plus, our premium membership offering; SoFi Coach, our AI-powered financial planning and insights product; SoFi Pay, our global remittance business; Growth, which supports our marketing enablement platforms; and more.

In this role, you will serve as a trusted partner to Member leadership, leading the business unit’s planning and operating cadence while helping teams translate strategy into measurable results. You will connect priorities across Member and the broader company, provide insights on business performance, drive cross-functional execution, and help ensure the Member team remains on track to achieve, and exceed, its objectives.

What you’ll do:

• Lead operations and operating cadence across Member’s diverse portfolio: Partner with leaders across SoFi Plus, SoFi Coach, SoFi Pay, Growth, and other Member businesses to establish effective meeting rhythms, maintain alignment on priorities, surface dependencies, and drive accountability across the Business Unit.

• Own quarterly and annual planning: Lead the Member Business Unit’s planning process in partnership with Finance, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Data Science, and business leaders. Set timelines and milestones, clarify requirements and ownership, coordinate inputs, and ensure planning materials are complete, cohesive, and executive-ready.

• Drive performance management and insights: Partner with Member teams to set meaningful OKRs, monitor progress against goals, and identify opportunities, risks, and performance trends. Build or oversee dashboards and analyses that explains what is happening, why, and what actions should follow.

• Connect strategy across the organization: Gather cross-functional dependencies, surface tradeoffs, and help align roadmaps and priorities across Member and the broader company. Connect the dots across teams to improve decision-making and execution.

• Serve as a strategic advisor to Member leadership: Maintain a deep understanding of the Member business, its objectives, and its role in SoFi’s broader strategy. Provide perspective on business health, organizational effectiveness, and opportunities to increase impact; represent the Member Business Unit on behalf of the Business Unit Leader as needed.

• Strengthen culture and team effectiveness: Partner with the People Business Partner and Member leadership to translate engagement survey feedback into actionable improvements, and drive initiatives that strengthen team health, culture, and performance.

• Lead executive communications: Develop clear, concise updates for Executive Staff, Member leadership, and other key stakeholders on business performance, strategic priorities, dependencies, risks, and progress against company and Member OKRs.

• Improve how the business operates: Identify opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen accountability, and improve team effectiveness. Develop recommendations and drive solutions from idea through implementation.

• Support high-impact strategic initiatives: Lead or contribute to special projects, business reviews, planning sessions, and offsites that advance Member’s objectives and SoFi’s mission.

• Use AI to amplify team impact: Identify and apply AI tools to accelerate analysis, synthesize information, improve decision-making, automate repeatable processes, and increase the efficiency and effectiveness of Member’s operating rhythms. Evaluate opportunities to adopt AI thoughtfully and responsibly across the business.

What you’ll need:

• 12+ years of experience in business operations, strategy, management consulting, chief of staff, or related roles; MBA preferred

• Experience in financial services or fintech strongly preferred

• Demonstrated ability to operate as a trusted advisor to senior leadership (VP+ level)

• Strong analytical skills (snowflake, spreadsheet modeling, Tableau, etc.) to independently pull and analyze data

• Experience working with AI tools for analysis and process automation

• Proven track record of leading cross-functional programs from ambiguity through execution

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex topics into concise executive-ready materials

• Experience with OKR frameworks, strategic planning processes, and operating cadences at scale

• Ability to context-switch rapidly and manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment

What it takes to succeed:

• You’re a full-stack operator: You can move fluidly from shaping strategy and clarifying priorities to building the plan, coordinating stakeholders, and driving execution through completion.

• You influence without authority: You build trust quickly and align senior leaders and cross-functional partners around shared objectives, even when priorities are competing or the path forward is not fully defined.

• You’re a data-driven storyteller: You use data to get to the answer, understand the “why” behind performance, and distill complex information into clear recommendations and executive-ready communications.

• You create structure from ambiguity: You bring clarity to open-ended problems, establish practical processes and operating rhythms, and help teams make progress when inputs, timelines, and ownership are evolving.

• You have a bias toward action: You balance strategic thinking with pragmatism, identify the highest-impact next steps, and follow through to ensure decisions turn into results.

• You can juggle multiple priorities and wear many hats: You’re comfortable shifting between planning, analysis, communications, problem-solving, and execution while staying focused on the work that matters most.

• You’re Member-first: You connect business decisions to the end-to-end member experience and understand how improving outcomes for members drives long-term business performance.

jobs.title: Clinical Trial Associate
jobs.location: South San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
Septerna is a biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, CA on a mission to develop life-changing medicines for patients with the vision to become the industry-leading G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-focused drug discovery company. The company’s Native Complex Platform™ recapitulates GPCRs with their native structure, function, and dynamics outside of the cellular context. This approach enables novel access to modern structural and screening technologies used in industrial-scale drug discovery for the entire class of GPCRs. Septerna has an emerging pipeline of GPCR-targeted small molecule programs, many in the Endocrinology space, with potential for growth to target many GPCRs that have been undruggable and unexploited to date.

We are excited to expand our multidisciplinary team of individuals focused on creating revolutionary medicines to address the unmet needs of patients. At Septerna we strive to embrace diversity of thought, expertise, and background through collaboration. To join our ambitious team, be prepared to bring your real self to work every day; grow and learn from a talented team of drug hunters, scientists, and business professionals; and contribute your passion, creativity, and energy to accomplish our mission. We share a fearless pursuit of ground-breaking innovations and cultivate an environment where our employees succeed by learning from each other and working as a team.

We are committed to the development of meaningful therapeutics for patients with indications of high unmet need. This is a tremendous opportunity to work with talented individuals on the frontlines of therapeutic discovery and development. You will directly help move therapies through preclinical research, positioning them for success in the clinic. The successful candidate will add their passion, unique talents, and expertise to a dynamic team motivated to discover new disease-modifying therapeutics for patients in a fast-paced environment.

For more information see: www.septerna.com.

About the Role:

We are looking for a highly motivated and detail-oriented Clinical Trial Associate to join our dynamic Clinical Operations team. Reporting to the Vice President of Clinical Operations, you will play a pivotal role in planning, executing, and managing clinical trials. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of life-changing treatments, while gaining exposure to various facets of clinical research in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

As a Clinical Trial Associate, you will provide critical support throughout the clinical trial lifecycle, ensuring compliance with industry standards and driving forward clinical excellence. With a focus on career development, you'll have the chance to grow within the organization and explore new avenues for advancement in Clinical Operations.

Key Responsibilities:

• Assist and support Clinical Trial Managers and CRA(s) in managing clinical trials, ensuring smooth execution from start-up to close-out including meeting agenda and meeting minutes, maintaining study trackers, filing documents, etc

• Liaise with clinical trial sites, vendors, CROs, and partners as appropriate, to maintain seamless communication and foster positive relationships.

• Support the team with administrative tasks, ensuring that all documentation is up-to-date and compliant with regulatory requirements.

• Ensure accurate and organized tracking of trial-related documentation, contributing to successful audits and regulatory submissions.

• Manage one or more study vendor(s)

• Prepare meeting agendas, create reports, and facilitate effective communication across all stakeholders.

• Assist in tracking clinical trial progress, from enrollment metrics to status updates, ensuring the project stays on target and within scope. Identify and escalate issues as appropriate.

• Proactively identify potential issues and collaborate with the study team to resolve them quickly, keeping trials on track.

• Assist with the collection and processing of investigator site and regulatory documents, adhering to FDA and international regulatory standards (such as GCP and ICH).

• Coordinate shipments of study-related materials, and ensure proper distribution to clinical sites.

• Prepare and maintain essential documents, including clinical study files, regulatory binders, and operational manuals.

• Help ensure smooth day-to-day operations by maintaining efficient filing systems, organizing clinical trial documentation, and supporting internal processes to optimize team productivity.

Why Join Us:

• At our company, your growth matters. This role offers ample opportunities to learn and advance your career in Clinical Operations.

• Be part of a passionate team working on groundbreaking clinical trials that could shape the future of healthcare. Your contributions will have a direct impact on improving lives.

• Work in a supportive and inclusive team where your voice is heard and your ideas matter. You'll have the chance to work alongside industry experts and build valuable relationships.

• We offer a competitive salary, benefits package, and a dynamic work culture that prioritizes work-life balance.

Qualifications:

• BA/BS in a related field or equivalent and 2+ years of industry experience in Clinical Operations (or equivalent experience without a degree).

• Strong understanding of clinical research regulatory requirements, including Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and International Conference on Harmonization (ICH).

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

• Ability to multitask, prioritize effectively, and maintain a keen attention to detail. Strong organizational and time management skills are essential.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams and stakeholders.

The anticipated salary range for candidates who will work in South San Francisco, CA is $110,000 - $125,000. Individual pay may vary based on additional factors, including, and without limitation, job-related skills, experience, work location and relevant education or training. As an intern on the IT team, you will provide advanced end-user technical support as part of Site Support and IT Operations. Serve as a technical escalation resource for complex endpoint, application, authentication, and connectivity issues. Coordinate with specialist teams and vendors to restore service, communicate clearly with users, and document repeatable solutions that reduce recurring incidents.

Role and Responsibilities

• Own complex incidents escalated from front-line support, including diagnosis, resolution, user communication, and complete ticket documentation.

• Troubleshoot Windows and macOS endpoints, enterprise applications, peripherals, VPN, Wi-Fi, and network connectivity issues.

• Resolve access and authentication issues involving Okta, Active Directory, and supported corporate accounts; coordinate authorization changes with the appropriate teams.

• Install, configure, and troubleshoot approved software; support endpoint updates and security patches through established processes.

• Perform advanced hardware diagnostics and coordinate repairs, replacements, or vendor support within approved scope.

• Identify recurring issues, document root causes and workarounds, and partner with endpoint engineering, networking, application, and security teams on durable fixes.

• Create and maintain knowledge articles, troubleshooting procedures, and escalation documentation; share technical guidance with front-line support staff.

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

As a Manager, Technical Account Management, you’ll lead the Technical Account Managers who serve as the persistent technical advisor embedded in Vercel’s marquee accounts, across AI agent platforms, large-scale migrations, and greenfield builds.

You’ll stay close to the accounts yourself, stepping into P1 and P2 escalations, reviewing architecture, and carrying a small set of strategic logos.

In your first year, success looks like a team driving real adoption depth on their accounts, strong retention on the book they cover, and an engagement model repeatable enough to hire into.

jobs.title: SOX AI Specialist (Contractor)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by automating and streamlining the work of advisory, audit, and tax practitioners at the world’s largest CPA firms. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We’re headquartered in San Francisco, California, and backed by top investors, including Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and others.

 
 


ABOUT THE ENGAGEMENT

We are seeking an experienced SOX and internal controls practitioner for a paid, short-term contract engagement. This is not a full-time role (at this time).

Over an initial engagement of 8–12 weeks, with the potential to extend, you will work directly with a small, cross-functional group of subject-matter experts, AI engineers, and product partners. You’ll help translate real-world SOX testing judgment into reliable, AI-assisted workflows. This is not a traditional client-delivery audit or attestation role. Your focus will be on prompting and refining AI agents to execute control testing and partnering closely with AI engineers to identify new engineering capabilities to enable better control testing.



Engagement type: Direct contractor

Initial term: 8–12 weeks, with potential to extend 

Start date: Immediate 

Time commitment: Approximately 40 hours per week 

Target rate: $60–$80 per hour, based on experience, with flexibility for an exceptional fit.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Partner closely with engineering, product, and design teams to translate real-world SOX testing processes into scalable product capabilities.

 - Co-develop AI agents with AI engineers to execute detailed SOX testing by translating SOX testing methodology into specific guidance, decision rules, and examples.

 - Work hands-on with AI agents: write and refine prompts, run controls and evidence through testing workflows, evaluate outputs, and document failure modes.

 - Analyze risk and control matrices and test plans to identify opportunities for improved agentic testing.

 - Develop stress-test scenarios, review and assess AI agent performance, and create detailed error analyses and evaluation criteria.

 
 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - At least four years of hands-on control testing experience in SOX compliance, internal audit, or internal controls, with direct responsibility for control design and testing.

 - Broad experience across a range of control types, industries, and firms, with clear expertise in business process control testing.

 - The ability to consistently explain why a test step, exception, or conclusion passes or fails and to turn that reasoning into clear evaluation criteria.

 - Strong written reasoning: you can explain workflows and decisions step by step and turn professional judgment into clear rules, edge cases, and review criteria.

 - A high degree of comfort and hands-on experience using AI tools, writing prompts, and working with agentic harnesses.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity, testing ideas quickly, and changing your approach when the evidence does not support it.

 - Availability for the expected time commitment during the initial engagement.

 
 


WHAT WE’D LOVE TO SEE

 - Experience at the senior or manager level reviewing SOX workpapers or coaching testers.

 - A CPA, CIA, or similar relevant credential.

jobs.title: VoIP Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Description

Lance (YC W26) develops autonomous AI agents that handle calls, close sales, and manage operations, enabling your team to focus on providing excellent guest experiences. Trusted by leading hotel groups across the U.S., Lance supports 50+ hotels with brands like Marriott, Hilton, and Hyatt. Combining AI agents with an all-in-one operating system for hotels covering front desk, housekeeping, maintenance, and sales, Lance integrates seamlessly with existing hotel software to make real-time decisions and efficiently manage complex tasks.

The role

You'll be Lance's first dedicated VoIP engineer and own telephony end to end. You'll decide how calls get in and out, how hotels get connected, and how we know it's working.

Every hotel brings a different phone system. You'll turn one-off integrations into a repeatable process by building the architecture, standards, tooling, and documentation. As Lance grows, you'll help shape the team that runs telephony.

What ownership means here

 - Make the architecture calls. Own telephony architecture, vendor choices, and tradeoffs. Be ready to explain why you made them.

 - Set the standards. Define what makes a hotel ready to go live and what makes a call healthy.

 - Build for other teams. Create the processes, checklists, and tooling that let others onboard and support hotels without you on every call.

 - Grow the function. When telephony needs more people, help define the roles and hire them.

What you'll do

 - Telephony architecture. Design how calls reach our AI agent and how they leave it. Evolve that architecture as we scale to hundreds of properties.

 - Hotel onboarding. Build the process and tooling that takes a property from first contact to live calls, then keep making it faster and safer.

 - PBX and carrier interoperability. Be the technical counterpart for hotel IT, phone vendors, carriers, and telephony partners across modern and decades-old systems.

 - Call transfers. Own handoffs from the agent to hotel staff and build safeguards that stop calls from looping back.

 - Call quality. Find and fix one-way audio, NAT and firewall issues, codec mismatches, jitter, and noise. Tune audio for speech recognition as well as human listeners.

 - Tenant isolation. Make sure every call reaches only the right hotel.

 - Observability and on-call. Build monitoring, alerting, and runbooks so we can spot failures before hotels do. Define how we respond to telephony incidents.

 - Numbering and compliance. Own number porting, E911, and caller ID (STIR/SHAKEN).

What we're looking for

 - 5+ years building or operating production VoIP systems with real carrier traffic and customers on the other end.

 - End-to-end ownership of a telephony system, including making the architecture decisions yourself.

 - Experience writing standards, runbooks, or processes that other people now follow.

 - Deep SIP knowledge: INVITE flows, SDP negotiation, transfers, authentication, and registration. You can read a packet capture or SIP trace without looking things up.

 - Hands-on experience with SBCs and SIP trunking: IP peering, number-based routing, TLS/SRTP, and NAT traversal.

 - Experience with programmable carriers: number provisioning, trunking, and porting.

 - Working knowledge of enterprise PBXs and patience working with hotel IT teams and phone vendors.

 - Strong networking fundamentals: UDP/TCP, RTP/RTCP, firewalls, and how media breaks across them.

 - You write production code and ship configuration and tooling through code review.

Nice to have

 - You've been the first hire in a function or built a team or process from scratch.

 - Open-source media servers and SIP proxies such as FreeSWITCH, Asterisk, or Kamailio.

 - Voice AI experience: latency budgets, barge-in, noise suppression, and how audio quality affects speech-to-text.

 - Hospitality telephony: PMS-to-PBX integrations, room-status codes, and call accounting.

 - Cloud networking and infrastructure as code.

 - Mobile VoIP on Android and iOS.

 - Compliance experience with E911, Kari's Law, call recording consent, or SOC 2.

First 90 days

 1. Days 1–30: Take ownership. Run the next hotel rollouts yourself. Document what's fragile, what's manual, and what's missing.

 2. Days 31–60: Set the standards. Define what a healthy call and a launch-ready hotel look like, and ship monitoring that checks both.

 3. Days 61–90: Make onboarding repeatable. Build tooling and a process someone else can run safely. Present your telephony roadmap for the next year.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Platform Security (All Levels)
jobs.description:
At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms—so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure.

Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users.

Our platform is trusted by over 7 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $260M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive—designed for the speed of modern AI development.

We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you.




APPLYING TO RENDER

We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team.

We especially encourage members of underrepresented groups in the tech community to apply and understand that not all successful candidates will meet each requirement listed.

Our interview process is unique to each role, and we value the candidate experience just as much as our customer experience. We hope your conversations with us reflect a thoughtful process that is illuminative, enjoyable, and respectful of your time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Render runs millions of customer workloads across our global infrastructure. Our Platform Security team makes sure that infrastructure is secure from threats and build the isolation our customers rely on to run their workloads safely. We are an engineering team. We build secure building blocks and systems for our infrastructure teams to move faster. You’ll write code and implement patterns that make the secure path the default and partner with other teams to work on areas such as patching, workload isolation and access management.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Linux and container vulnerability management and build autonomous systems to patch our fleet fast and safely.

 - Harden Kubernetes, containers, and the Linux kernel.

 - Build access controls to maintain least privilege into our most sensitive systems.

 - Protect our supply chain from vulnerabilities and malware. This includes CI, base images and registries

 - Build detections for anomalous activities on our hosts or in our cloud platforms.

 - Implement new architectures for managing and rotating internal and customer secrets.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong software engineering skills, you have worked on production infrastructure.

 - Experience securing cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes at scale.

 - Deep knowledge of Linux.

 - Strong judgment toward security risks and tradeoffs.

 - A sense of ownership to take projects from idea to shipped.

 - Empathy for our engineering team and our customers.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with any of the technologies the Render product runs on: Go, Typescript, Kubernetes, Postgres, Terraform, Temporal.

 - Experience with sandboxing or virtualization technologies.

 - Experience with detection engineering including building and operating a SIEM.

 - Contributions to the security community through research, talks, or open source.

If this role excites you but you don’t meet every single requirement, we’d still love to hear from you—your unique experience might be just what we need.




BENEFITS

 - 4 weeks of paid vacation.

 - 14 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all parents to bond with a newly born, adopted, or fostered child. We will also work with you to create a supportive plan of return.

jobs.title: Data Integrity Administrator
jobs.description:
Salary is determined based on experience and the Foundation’s structured pay bands, which include steps for growth and performance. Please see the “Pay” section for more details.

Priority Application Deadline: December 11, 2026

FLSA Status: Exempt

Starting Salary: $92,330 - $107,718 (Step I - Step II)

Work Location: Remote

About the Position

As the Data Integrity Administrator, you will play a key role in advancing our mission by leading the OHSU Foundation’s data governance and data quality program, ensuring constituent, gift, prospect, engagement, and related advancement data are accurate, complete, consistent, clearly defined, and fit for use. You will be collaborating closely with Gift & Data Administration, Data Solutions & Insights, Prospect Development, Information Technology, and other teams across the Foundation.

We know there’s no such thing as a perfect candidate. If your experience isn’t a direct match for everything we’ve listed, but you believe your skills and background align with the role, we encourage you to apply.

What You’ll Be Doing

Data Governance Leadership

• You will lead the Foundation’s operational data governance framework, meetings, and measures of effectiveness in partnership with the Managing Senior Director of Gift & Data Administration.

• You will lead the Data Quality Champions, a cross-functional network of data users, stewards and change champions who represent team needs, reinforce standards, and provide feedback on adoption, effectiveness, and quality of our data.

• You will lead the Change Advisory Council, preparing decision-ready materials, documenting approvals, and maintaining an accessible decision log.

• You will partner with IT and Data Solutions & Insights to develop and maintain a data glossary with definitions, business rules, stewardship assignments, and standards for entry, maintenance, access, use and retention.

Data Quality, Reconciliation, and Issue Management

• You will own the centralized data quality issue intake and triage process.

• You will partner with System Admins to translate approved business requirements into technical changes.

• You will establish and monitor data quality scorecards across key dimensions of the CRM (Ignite) for accuracy, completeness, consistency and timeliness.

• You will analyze trends and recurring defects to distinguish individual corrections from systemic process, integration, or configuration issues.

Team Leadership and Service Delivery

• You will supervise, coach, and develop two Data Integrity and Reconciliation Analysts.

• You will establish clear priorities, standards, documentation practices and development goals for the team.

• You will maintain a service-oriented team culture that listens to business partners, explains findings clearly, and focuses on durable solutions rather than isolated corrections.

Change Management, Communication, and Data Stewardship

• You will translate complex governance decisions into clear guidance for Foundation staff: what is changing, why it matters, who is affected, what action is required, and where documentation lives.

• You will partner with OHSU Foundation Trainers to develop practical training, documentation and resources that strengthen data literacy and the consistent use of Ignite.

• You will promote responsible handling of confidential donor information and separation of fundraising data from protected health information, partnering with privacy, compliance, and legal experts when needed.

Who You Are

• You’re able to facilitate cross-functional groups, clarify ownership, resolve ambiguity, and influence without direct authority.

• Your strong process-analysis skills include workflow mapping, requirements gathering, RACI development, risk assessment, testing, and documentation.

• You’re able to communicate complex data issues plainly to technical and non-technical audiences and convert decisions into practical standards, procedures, training, and communications.

• You’re someone with high judgment and discretion in handling confidential donor, prospect, and institutional information in a healthcare and/or higher education environment.

• You’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, with the ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues and partners from varied backgrounds and lived experiences.

Required Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in information management, data analytics, business, healthcare administration, nonprofit management, information systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience

• Seven or more years of progressively responsible experience in data governance, data quality, data administration, advancement services, CRM operations, business analysis, or a closely related field

• Three or more years of experience leading staff, projects, or cross-functional governance initiatives; direct supervisory experience strongly preferred

• Demonstrated experience designing or operating data quality controls, reconciliation processes, issue intake and prioritization, business glossaries, definition management, or stewardship programs

• Experience working in healthcare fundraising, academic or higher education advancement, or a comparable environment involving sensitive constituent, donor, patient-adjacent, or institutional data

Preferred Experience

• Significant experience in an academic medical center, healthcare foundation, or similarly complex advancement environment

• Experience with Salesforce along with data quality, visualization, ticketing, metadata, or governance tools

• Professional development or certification in data governance, data management, change management, project management, or process improvement, such as DAMA CDMP, Prosci, PMP, Lean, or Six Sigma

Working Conditions

• Prolonged computer use for data review, documentation, analysis, testing, and virtual meetings

• Primarily remote work schedule with some in-office time expected during specific annual touchpoints (summer all staff retreat, etc)

• Occasional work outside normal business hours may be required for time-sensitive releases, reconciliations, or system changes

Salary

$92,330—$107,718 USD

Pay

Salary is dependent on experience. Each salary band is broken into three "steps," which correspond with an employee’s experience/tenure, proficiency and performance in that specific role. New employees will typically start at step I of our pay band to allow for later growth, although more experienced candidates may be eligible to start at step II or III. The OHSU Foundation has a structured process for determining starting compensation, taking into account years of related experience, applicable skills, knowledge and abilities, market parity and internal equity.

Benefits

The OHSU Foundation also offers an exceptional benefits package including:

• Comprehensive medical and dental insurance.

• Pension program (The Foundation contributes 12% of your annual salary to a pension);

• 22 days of paid vacation, 11 paid holidays, 1 float holiday and 2 days of volunteer time off;

• Professional development dollars for each employee;

• Hybrid work allowance and much more!

Plus, we have a flexible work environment for those who prefer a hybrid work schedule, and we close early on Fridays during the summer. Want to learn more about our other amazing benefits? Check out our benefits page to learn more about our benefits.

Please note that benefits may vary for employees residing outside of Oregon, Washington, Arkansas, Alaska, Arizona and Nevada due to state-specific regulations and coverage differences. Employees located outside of these states may be required to work through a Professional Employer Organization (PEO).

Our Core Values

Every relationship we cultivate, every gift we secure, every action we take advances OHSU’s mission for excellence in education, research and scholarship, clinical practice and community service.

Alignment

Compassion

Equity

Integrity

Collaboration

Impact

If you require support or reasonable accommodation during the application or recruitment process, please submit a request through our Accommodation Request Form.

The OHSU Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Employer

The OHSU Foundation is committed to being an equal opportunity, affirmative action organization. In keeping with our beliefs and values, no applicant will face discrimination or harassment on the basis of any protected class status, including color, age, current or future military status, disability (physical or mental), gender, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status or any other status protected by law.

The OHSU Foundation, as required by law, is making available a copy of Employee Rights and Responsibilities under the Family and Medical Leave Act.

The OHSU Foundation participates in E-Verify. By law we are required to make available the Notice of E-Verify Participation and the Right to Work.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Nonclinical Safety and Portfolio Strategy
jobs.description:
AbbVie’s Development Biological Sciences organization is seeking a Senior Director, Nonclinical Safety and Portfolio Strategy to set enterprise direction for nonclinical safety and influence the highest-impact R&D and portfolio decisions. The role is accountable for future-state strategy, portfolio risk leadership, organizational capability, and scientific positions that protect patients, accelerate the pipeline, and strengthen AbbVie’s long-term competitive advantage.

The successful candidate will be an internally and externally recognized leader who combines exceptional scientific judgment, enterprise perspective, and executive influence. The individual will shape governance decisions, mobilize leaders across functions, represent AbbVie in consequential external forums, and build the talent and capabilities required for current and emerging drug modalities.

Key Responsibilities

• Define and drive the enterprise vision and multi-year strategy for nonclinical safety, aligning functional priorities, capabilities, investments, and external partnerships with AbbVie’s R&D and portfolio imperatives.
• Serve as an executive scientific advisor to senior R&D leaders and governance bodies, influencing portfolio prioritization, investment, development pathways, and risk acceptance for the most consequential assets.
• Maintain strategic oversight for the highest-complexity, highest-value, or precedent-setting programs, ensuring that safety strategy is integrated with clinical benefit, regulatory feasibility, CMC considerations, and long-term asset value.
• Establish enterprise positions and decision principles across small molecules, biologics, ADCs, cell and gene therapies, and emerging modalities, adapting approaches across oncology, neuroscience, immunology, and other therapeutic areas.
• Lead AbbVie’s nonclinical safety strategy for major transactions and external innovation, providing decisive recommendations on partnerships, in-licensing, acquisitions, and portfolio entry or exit decisions.
• Direct strategy for pivotal global regulatory interactions and precedent-setting submissions; align senior leaders on risk posture and represent AbbVie with health authorities when issues have broad portfolio or enterprise implications.
• Create and sponsor future-state scientific, digital, data, and AI-enabled capabilities that improve translation, prediction, evidence integration, and decision velocity across the organization.
• Shape industry practice and regulatory science through leadership in consortia, professional organizations, advisory groups, and strategic collaborations; strengthen AbbVie’s external scientific reputation and influence.
• Lead enterprise-wide initiatives that transcend functional boundaries, resolve competing priorities, and deliver sustained value for the pipeline and organization.
• Build organizational capability through workforce strategy, succession planning, differentiated development, and deployment of senior talent. Lead leaders and hold teams accountable for enterprise outcomes.

Leadership Responsibilities

• Sets enterprise direction and makes AbbVie-first decisions across competing priorities.
• Inspires leaders around a shared purpose and aligns diverse stakeholders without relying on authority.
• Balances immediate portfolio outcomes with long-term capability and competitive advantage.
• Creates new value by connecting scientific, regulatory, technological, and business perspectives.
• Builds leaders, succession depth, and a culture of accountability, inclusion, and scientific excellence.

Location

• North Chicago, Lake County, IL is primary preference. Other AbbVie locations considered in Worcester, MA; San Francisco, CA; or Irvine, CA in a Hybrid model.

• PhD or DVM required.
• 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical industry experience, including leadership of complex nonclinical safety programs and portfolio strategy.
• Demonstrated impact across discovery through registration, with experience influencing major R&D, regulatory, and portfolio decisions.
• Broad expertise across modalities and therapeutic areas, with deep expertise in at least one strategically relevant domain preferred.
• Extensive experience leading global health authority interactions and shaping regulatory strategy for complex or precedent-setting issues.
• Recognized internal and external scientific leadership, executive communication, enterprise influence, and demonstrated development of senior talent.
